title.rendered: 50 Stunning 4K Dynamic Island Wallpapers for iPhone

content.rendered:
These wallpapers work the Dynamic Island into the artwork, whether a character hangs from the pill or a dark background blends it away. The gallery supports iPhone 14 Pro and Pro Max and newer models that include Dynamic Island, including iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

The 50 downloads keep a tall iPhone shape, but their resolutions vary. Each button now shows the file’s pixel size so you can pick the largest version available.

What Is a Dynamic Island Wallpaper?

These backgrounds place a character, object, or graphic around the pill-shaped cutout. iPhone 18 Pro models have a smaller Dynamic Island than earlier Pro models, so some older artwork may sit a little differently. Check the Lock Screen preview and adjust the crop before saving.

The files are portrait images in three sizes: 1109 × 2400, 1170 × 2532, and 1179 × 2556 pixels. iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max displays are 1206 × 2622 and 1320 × 2868 pixels, so iOS enlarges these downloads to fit. Choose the largest version available for the sharpest result. The result? Your iPhone’s screen feels more dynamic, personalized, and visually appealing.

Tips for choosing the perfect Dynamic Island wallpaper

  • Pick the largest file size listed under a design. A close aspect ratio helps prevent cropping, but more pixels keep the image sharper on larger screens.
  • Keep the main artwork clear of the clock and widgets on your Lock Screen.
  • If the artwork points to or wraps around the Dynamic Island, check the preview on your own model before applying it. The cutout is smaller on iPhone 18 Pro models.
  • Dark backgrounds help the pill blend in; bright lines and characters make it stand out.

Note: Each Download button lists the image dimensions. Save the file to Photos before setting it as wallpaper.

Best Dynamic Island Wallpapers by category

1. Cute & Whimsical Dynamic Island Wallpapers

Playful, charming designs featuring adorable characters and lighthearted scenes that bring a smile to your iPhone screen.

Cute Bear

Add a touch of charm and whimsy as a cute bear peeks out from behind the Dynamic Island on your iPhone. Embrace the magic of this wallpaper and add an extra layer of enchantment to your device.

Download

Minions Antics

Another fun Minions wallpaper from the Despicable Me movies. It looks like one minion is holding onto the Dynamic Island on your iPhone. Three Minions are standing at the bottom, looking up with fun expressions. Overall, it creates a fun and playful scene on your screen.

Download

Minions Fun

This Minion-themed Dynamic Island wallpaper will give you a heavy dose of fun every time you unlock your iPhone. Tap the download button to watch these lovable characters bring life to your device with their antics.

Download

Cute Cat

This adorable cat-themed Dynamic Island wallpaper is a must-have for all feline enthusiasts. Tap the download button to add a cute, furry companion to your screen and brighten your day.

Download

Cats and Mouse

We don’t want to play a cat-and-mouse game with you. All we want to do is share this cat-and-mouse wallpaper with you.

Download

Scrat from the Ice Age

Why not bring some chaos to your iPhone? Here’s Scrat, the iconic squirrel from Ice Age, hanging from your iPhone’s Dynamic Island! A must-have for Ice Age fans and anyone looking for a fun wallpaper!

Download

Shinchan

Watching Shinchan was and still is an emotional experience! To keep it up, you can download this Shinchan wallpaper that uses Dynamic Island creatively.

Download

Wreck-it Ralph

This vibrant iPhone wallpaper showcases Ralph, the iconic character from Ralph Breaks the Internet, in his signature red plaid shirt and overalls. Perfect for fans of the animated classic, this wallpaper combines playful energy with a modern design.

2. Pop Culture & Cartoons Dynamic Island Wallpapers

Wallpapers inspired by iconic movies, TV shows, and beloved cartoon characters—perfect for fans who want to showcase their favorites.

The Incredibles

Let’s have some family fun with this black wallpaper for your iPhone inspired from Incredibles movies. A large red spotlight shining down from the top creates a dramatic effect. Download this wallpaper and let the Incredible Family pop up on your iPhone display.

Download

Classic Muppets (Bert)

Do you also love the classic Muppets from Sesame Street? Download this wallpaper featuring Bert with his mad expression. The fun part is his iconic straight eyebrows will replace your Dynamic Island, making your iPhone Lock Screen unique.

Download

Simpson’s Burger Catch

This Dynamic Island wallpaper features playful Simpson reaching up with his mouth wide open, ready to catch a large burger falling towards him. The contrasting backdrop indeed catches the eye. This fun wallpaper is perfect for adding a touch of humor to your iPhone’s screen.

Let’s get back childhood nostalgia with this cute Doraemon wallpaper for your iPhone Dynamic Island. The red vibrant wallpaper with the cartoon logo looks beautiful. Tap the download button to adorn it on your Home Screen.

3. Superhero Dynamic Island Wallpapers

Aesthetic Outdoors

This aesthetic Dynamic Island wallpaper will infuse your iPhone with a touch of elegance and style. Its captivating design will give your device a unique and eye-catching look. If you’re a fan of the outdoors, tap the download button now!

Futuristic Cyberpunk

Step into the future with this electrifying wallpaper with cyberpunk vibes. Whether you’re a fan of retro-futurism or modern digital art, this wallpaper is sure to turn heads and give your iPhone a distinctive, futuristic edge.

Black Stack

Calling out the black wallpaper lovers! This sleek wallpaper features a mesmerizing pattern of Dynamic Island-shaped pills aligned in a stack. Designed for tech-savvy iPhone users, it provides a minimalist yet high-tech vibe.

5. Nature & Scenery Dynamic Island Wallpapers

Serene landscapes, sunsets, and scenic elements that bring a touch of the outdoors and relaxation to your device.

Summer Sunset

I don’t know what you did last Summer. But this Summer, you definitely need to have this sunset wallpaper on your iPhone. It’s creative and aspirational at the same time!

Ocean View

If you like the vast blue oceans and sunsets, this wallpaper is ideal. It takes you to a breathtaking coastal landscape. For more stunning options, explore our ocean wallpapers for iPhone and get the beach vibes.

If you love cosmic themes, you’ll also enjoy browsing our space wallpapers for iPhone for even more out-of-this-world designs.

7. Fun & Playful Dynamic Island Wallpapers

Lively, quirky, and energetic designs that add a sense of movement and excitement to your Dynamic Island experience.

Walking Robot

Where to Find More Dynamic Island Wallpapers: Try These Apps

For more choices, browse these iPhone wallpaper apps. Their catalogs change, so search for “Dynamic Island” or “notch” and preview a design before saving it.

  • Vellum Wallpapers: Curated wallpaper packs and a daily image.
  • Walli: Wallpapers from independent artists.
  • Zedge: A large wallpaper library with search.
  • Backdrops: Original designs in categories such as minimal, abstract, and pop culture.
  • Unsplash: A photo library rather than a dedicated wallpaper catalog.

Tip: Search for “Dynamic Island” within these apps, or browse categories like “notch,” “pill,” or “cutout” for the best fit!

How to Set a Dynamic Island Wallpaper on Your iPhone

Setting up your new wallpaper is quick and easy:

  1. Download a wallpaper and save the image to Photos.
  2. Open Settings and tap Wallpaper.
  3. Tap Add New Wallpaper, then choose Photos and select the image.
  4. Adjust the crop in the preview so the artwork lines up with Dynamic Island.
  5. Tap Add, then choose Set as Wallpaper Pair or Customize Home Screen.

Use the preview to line up characters and graphics with the cutout before saving.

Tip: Some wallpapers are designed specifically for the Lock Screen, while others shine on the Home Screen. Experiment to find what works best for you!

Final thoughts

The Dynamic Island is more than just a notch—it’s an opportunity to express your style and creativity. With the right wallpaper, you can make your iPhone truly stand out. Try a few different looks, play with colors and themes, and enjoy the endless possibilities!

mainEntity.name: Can I disable Smart Stack on my Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Smart Stack is a built-in watchOS feature. Rather than disabling the entire feature, you can remove unwanted widgets, pin the ones you need, and adjust the available suggestion settings.

mainEntity.name: How many widgets can I add to Smart Stack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple doesn't specify a universal maximum number of widgets in its user guide. The available selection depends on compatible apps and widgets. Add the ones you find useful rather than following an arbitrary widget limit.

mainEntity.name: Can I use third-party widgets in Smart Stack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Compatible third-party apps can provide widgets for Smart Stack. The available widgets depend on the app and its support for your watchOS version.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Smart Stack and complications?

title.rendered: How to use Visual Intelligence on iPhone to translate, search, and ask ChatGPT

content.rendered:
Apple first introduced Visual Intelligence with iOS 18.2, a feature that could recognize what your iPhone’s camera saw in real time. With iOS 27, Apple takes it a step further. Visual Intelligence is now closely integrated with Siri AI, giving the iPhone a much better understanding of what is in front of the camera and what is displayed on the screen.

Here’s a full guide on how to use Visual Intelligence on your iPhone.

What is Visual Intelligence?

Visual Intelligence is an Apple Intelligence-powered feature that combines on-device AI with real-time visual understanding. It debuted with the iPhone 16 series and requires at least an A17 Pro chip with an advanced Neural Engine for fast, private processing.

With it, your iPhone can recognize and extract details from what your camera or screen shows—from identifying a plant to translating a menu, finding products online, or getting instant help from ChatGPT and Siri AI.

In iOS 27, Visual Intelligence is more closely connected to Siri. It can:

  • Identify objects and places
  • Ask questions about something in front of the camera
  • Search the web for visually similar images
  • Recognize plants and animals
  • Read, summarize, and translate text
  • Get information about businesses
  • Analyze food and provide nutritional information
  • Interact with restaurant bills
  • Extract information from documents and cards
  • Turn information from flyers into calendar events
  • Take actions based on what the camera sees

Apple also lets Visual Intelligence work with screenshots, so you don’t need to physically point your camera at something if the information is already on your iPhone.

Which iPhones support Visual Intelligence?

Visual Intelligence requires an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone.

Apple says Apple Intelligence on iOS 27 is available on:

  • iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16e, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max
  • iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max
  • iPhone Duo

Apple Intelligence availability can vary depending on the device, language, and region.

If you are unsure whether your iPhone supports the feature:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Apple Intelligence & Siri or Siri.
  3. Check whether Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone.

How to access Visual Intelligence on iPhone

iOS 27 gives several ways to launch Visual Intelligence.

Method 1: Use Siri Mode in Camera

If you have Siri AI enabled, this is the most direct way to use Visual Intelligence.

  1. Open the Camera app.
  2. Swipe through the camera modes until you reach Siri.
  3. Point your iPhone camera at whatever you want to understand.
  4. Tap the Siri button to learn about what is in the frame.

For example, I can point the camera at an unfamiliar object and tap the Siri button to get information about it. Then swipe down on the response and continue the conversation with follow-up questions.

Method 2: Use Camera Control

If your iPhone has the Camera Control button, press and hold it to let Visual Intelligence analyze the scene, then choose one of the suggested actions or ask a question.

First, you need to set it up:

  1. Open Settings on your iPhone.
  2. Select Camera and tap Camera Control.
  3. Scroll down and toggle on Press and Hold under the Launch Visual Intelligence section.

This remains one of the quickest ways to access Visual Intelligence on supported iPhones.

Method 3: Use the Action Button

If your iPhone doesn’t have Camera Control, you can assign Visual Intelligence to the Action button on supported models.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Action Button.
  3. Swipe through the available options.
  4. Select Visual Intelligence.
  5. Press and hold the Action button whenever you want to use it.

Method 4: Add Visual Intelligence to the Lock Screen

You can also customize your Lock Screen to add Visual Intelligence as a control.

  1. Unlock your iPhone with Face ID and touch and hold your Lock Screen.
  2. Tap Customize.
  3. Tap the minus button on the control you want to replace.
  4. Then tap the plus sign and select Visual Intelligence from the available controls.
  5. Tap Done.

This is particularly useful when I want to analyze something quickly without navigating through multiple menus.

Method 5: Add Visual Intelligence to Control Center

You can also launch it from Control Center.

  1. Swipe down from the top-right corner of your iPhone.
  2. Look for the Visual Intelligence control.
  3. Tap it to launch the feature.

If you don’t see it, tap the + button to customize Control Center and add the Visual Intelligence control.

How to use Visual Intelligence on iPhone

The real appeal of Visual Intelligence isn’t simply recognizing objects. What makes iOS 27 interesting is that the feature can turn what the camera sees into an action.

Here are some of the most useful things you can do.

1. Ask Siri about anything in front of your camera

This is one of the biggest changes in iOS 27.

Instead of simply identifying an object, I can ask a question about it. For example, I can point my camera at a cricket ball and ask: “How do you play cricket?”

Siri AI can identify the object and continue the conversation with a follow-up answer.

To try it:

  1. Open Camera.
  2. Switch to Siri mode.
  3. Point the camera at an object.
  4. Tap the Ask button on the left.
  5. Type or dictate your question.
  6. Wait for Siri’s response.

You can continue asking questions without starting over. Also, all these conversations are available in the Siri app for future reference.

This makes Visual Intelligence feel much more like an interactive assistant rather than a simple visual search tool.

2. Identify plants and animals

Visual Intelligence can recognize plants and animals through the camera.

To use it:

  1. Open Camera.
  2. Enter Siri mode or launch Visual Intelligence using your preferred shortcut.
  3. Point your camera at the plant or animal.
  4. Tap the suggested identification or tap the Siri button to know what you’re looking at.
  5. Follow the results for additional information.

If the system isn’t confident about an identification, treat the result as a suggestion rather than a guaranteed answer.

3. Identify places and businesses

Visual Intelligence can also help when you’re walking around a new area.

Point the camera at a business or location, and Visual Intelligence can provide relevant information about it, depending on what’s available in your region.

For supported businesses, you may see details such as:

  • Business information
  • Opening hours
  • Website
  • Contact information
  • Menu or ordering options
  • Other relevant actions

4. Get nutritional information from food

This is one of the more interesting iOS 27 additions.

Point your iPhone camera at food or a meal, and Visual Intelligence can provide information about it, including nutritional information and ingredients when the system can determine them.

To try it:

  1. Open Camera.
  2. Switch to Siri mode.
  3. Point the camera at your meal or food.
  4. Look for a suggested action or tap Ask.
  5. Ask something such as, “What is this food?” or “What can you tell me about this meal?”

The results are meant to provide useful information, not replace professional dietary or medical advice.

5. Split a restaurant bill

Visual Intelligence can now do more than read a restaurant receipt. With the updated Wallet app in iOS 27, Siri can offer a Split Bill option when you point your camera at a receipt.

To use it:

  1. Open Camera.
  2. Switch to Siri mode.
  3. Point your camera at the restaurant check.
  4. Wait for the suggested action.
  5. Tap Split Bill with Apple Cash if it appears.
  6. Follow the on-screen instructions to divide the bill.

The exact payment options depend on region and service availability.

6. Search for similar products and images

Visual Intelligence can perform a visual search when you want to find similar items online, similar to Google Lens.

For example, if I see a pair of shoes, bag, piece of furniture, or gadget I like, I can point my camera at it and search for visually similar results. You can also directly buy the product from the search results.

  1. Open Visual Intelligence.
  2. Point your camera at the object.
  3. Tap the Search button on the right.
  4. Review the visually similar results.
  5. You can also draw a circle to highlight the product you want to search.

This is particularly useful when I don’t know the name of the product I’m looking at.

7. Translate text with Visual Intelligence

Visual Intelligence can understand text through the camera and provide actions such as translation.

To translate text:

  1. Launch Visual Intelligence.
  2. Point your camera at the text.
  3. Let your iPhone analyze it or tap the Siri button.
  4. Choose the Translate option when it appears and tap Continue.
  5. Then tap on any text to listen to the translation or copy it. You can also change the translation language from here.

I often use this feature for signs, menus, labels, notices, and other printed text when traveling. No need to open the Translate app separately!

Visual Intelligence can also provide options for summarizing or reading text aloud when appropriate.

8. Summarize text you see

You don’t always need to read a long notice or document yourself.

Point your camera at the text, and Visual Intelligence can offer a Summarize and Read Aloud action.

This can be useful for:

  • Notices
  • Documents
  • Posters
  • Instructions
  • Long printed messages
  • Information sheets

The available actions depend on what Visual Intelligence detects.

9. Turn a flyer into a calendar event

Visual Intelligence can recognize event information from posters and flyers and help you add it to Calendar. This is much faster than manually typing the event name, date, time, and location.

To use it:

  1. Point your iPhone camera at the flyer or poster.
  2. Launch Visual Intelligence.
  3. Wait for the event information to be recognized.
  4. Tap the Add to Calendar option to create the event.
  5. Review the pre-filled details, such as the event title, dates, and location. You may also add invitees, reminder alerts, and other relevant details.
  6. Once satisfied, tap the checkmark to add it to your calendar.

Similarly, the feature also helps me add contacts from visiting cards.

Also read: I tried the Calendar app in iOS 27. These new features actually save time

Visual Intelligence also works with your iPhone screen

This is where Visual Intelligence becomes particularly useful.

You don’t have to point your camera at everything. If something is already displayed on your iPhone, you can use screenshot-based Visual Intelligence to understand it.

For example, I can use it on a product page, social media post, website, document, photo, message, screenshot of an app, and much more. Apple provides a dedicated Visual Intelligence experience for content on the iPhone screen.

Use Visual Intelligence on a Screenshot

  1. Open the content you want to analyze.
  2. Quickly press and release the Side button + Volume Up buttons together.
  3. Your iPhone takes a screenshot and opens the preview with Visual Intelligence tools.
  4. Depending on what’s on the screen, choose Ask, Search, or another suggested action. Siri AI can use on-screen awareness to answer questions and take actions based on screen content.
  5. Highlight a specific object if you only want to analyze part of the screenshot.

The tools shown at the bottom can change depending on the content in your screenshot.

The best feature is the ability to highlight an object on the screen. Suppose I’m looking at a screenshot containing several products, but I only want information about one of them. In such a case, simply take a screenshot and highlight the specific object.

Visual Intelligence can then search for that specific item rather than treating the entire screenshot as a single image. This is especially useful when comparing products or researching something I see on social media.

How Visual Intelligence works with ChatGPT

If you’ve used Visual Intelligence in earlier iOS versions, you may remember seeing an Ask option that handed questions to ChatGPT.

That integration hasn’t disappeared from Apple’s broader Apple Intelligence experience, but the iOS 27 Visual Intelligence workflow is more tightly connected to Siri AI.

If you still want to use ChatGPT for some queries, here’s how:

  1. Open Siri mode in Camera or take a screenshot of the content.
  2. Tap the Ask button and then enter this query: “Ask ChatGPT to tell me what this is”
  3. For the first time, it will prompt you to enable ChatGPT. Tap Turn On on the prompt.
  4. Then follow the one-screen instructions to enable the extension.
  5. Now, again enter your query added with “Ask ChatGPT,” and ChatGPT will continue the conversation.

The Siri app saves such conversations as well.

Change Visual Intelligence settings in iOS 27

Apple has added settings that let you control how Visual Intelligence behaves.

To find them:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Siri.
  3. Depending on your device and configuration, you can find settings such as:
    • Highlight to Search: Enable it to let Siri AI automatically search the web when you highlight something while using Siri mode in Camera or screenshots.
    • Automatic Visual Look Up: This allows your iPhone to automatically identify objects and places that appear in screenshots.

These options are useful if you want Visual Intelligence to be more proactive.

Visual Intelligence vs Visual Look Up: What’s the difference?

These two features can sound confusing because both can identify things.

Visual Look Up is Apple’s traditional image-recognition feature. It can recognize certain objects, animals, plants, landmarks, laundry symbols, car dashboard signs, and other visual content.

Visual Intelligence is broader. It combines Apple’s visual understanding with Apple Intelligence to let you search, ask questions, summarize information, translate text, and take actions based on what your camera or screen shows.

In iOS 27, Visual Intelligence also works closely with Siri AI, making it more conversational.

Things to keep in mind

Visual Intelligence is powerful, but I wouldn’t treat every result as authoritative. AI-generated information can sometimes be incomplete or incorrect, especially when the camera can’t clearly see the subject.

I also need to remember that feature availability varies by:

  • iPhone model
  • Region
  • Language
  • Apple Intelligence availability
  • Siri AI availability
  • Third-party service availability

Apple specifically notes that Apple Intelligence features aren’t available in every language or region, and Siri AI is currently offered as a beta feature on iOS 27.

For anything involving health, nutrition, finances, or other important decisions, I would verify the result using a reliable source rather than relying on Visual Intelligence alone.

Final thoughts

Visual Intelligence has come a long way since Apple introduced it.

In earlier versions of iOS, I mostly thought of it as a smart camera feature that could recognize objects, translate text, identify plants, or search for products. iOS 26 expanded the idea by letting Visual Intelligence understand what was on my screen.

With iOS 27, Apple takes the next step by bringing Visual Intelligence deeper into Siri and the Camera app. I can now ask Siri what I’m looking at, follow up with another question, search for similar images, or take an action based on what my iPhone sees.

If Apple continues improving Siri AI and Visual Intelligence in future updates, I think this could become one of the most useful parts of Apple Intelligence. What do you think about this feature? Let me know in the comments below!

  • ChatGPT vs Claude: My Real Experience

  • How to create a memory movie with Apple Intelligence on your iPhone

His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: I tried Live Translation with AirPods on iOS 27: here’s how it actually works

content.rendered:
The first time I tried Apple’s Live Translation with AirPods in iOS 26, the idea felt almost too futuristic: someone speaks another language, and I hear what they’re saying in my own language through my earbuds.

With iOS 27 and the latest Apple Intelligence features, Apple has continued expanding this feature, making it available on more AirPods models and supporting more languages. If the other person doesn’t have compatible AirPods, you can still use your iPhone to show or play the translated version of your response.

Here’s everything you need to know about Live Translation on AirPods, including the compatible iPhones and AirPods, supported languages, setup process, and how to use it during a real conversation.

What is Live Translation on AirPods and how does it work?

Live Translation is an Apple Intelligence feature that lets compatible AirPods translate what another person is saying into your preferred language in real time.

The experience is designed to be hands-free. Instead of repeatedly typing or looking at your iPhone, you can listen to the conversation through your AirPods while the Translate app provides a transcript on your iPhone.

Here’s how it works:

  1. The other person speaks in their language.
  2. Your AirPods and iPhone capture the conversation.
  3. Your iPhone processes the translation.
  4. You hear the translated speech through your AirPods.
  5. The Live tab in the Translate app can show a transcript of what was said.
  6. You can respond in your language.
  7. Your iPhone can show the translated response to the other person or play it aloud through its speaker.

This makes conversations smoother, whether you’re traveling, on a call, or speaking with someone in person.

Prerequisites

Before you can use Live Translation on your AirPods, make sure you meet these requirements:

  • AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, or AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation, AirPods 5 (both models), AirPods Max 2 updated to the latest firmware.
  • iPhone 15 Pro or later running iOS 26 or newer.
  • The Apple Translate app installed on your iPhone.
  • Apple Intelligence enabled on your iPhone.
  • Supported languages downloaded to your iPhone

Apple notes that availability can vary by language and region.

Supported languages

Currently in iOS 27, Live Translation supports these languages:

  • English (US and UK)
  • French
  • German
  • Italian
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese (Brazil)
  • Spanish (Spain)
  • Chinese (Mandarin, Simplified)
  • Chinese (Mandarin, Traditional)

Apple may add more language support in upcoming updates.

How to download languages for Live Translation

For Live Translation to work, you’ll need to download language models in advance. For example, if someone is speaking Spanish and you want to hear English, download both Spanish and English.

  1. Put on your AirPods and connect them to your iPhone.
  2. Now, open Settings → [Your Name] AirPods near the top of the screen.
  3. Here, locate and tap Live Translation (Beta).
  4. Next, select the languages you want to download.

Once downloaded, the entire translation process happens on-device to keep all conversation data private.

How to set up Live Translation on AirPods

Unlike Adaptive Audio, Live Translation isn’t enabled by default. Here’s how to set it up:

  1. Wear your AirPods and connect them to your iPhone.
  2. Now, open the Translate app and tap Live at the bottom.
  3. Under Their Language, select the language the other person is speaking.
  4. Under Your Language, select the language you want to hear through your AirPods.

This gives you full control over the conversation settings, including the languages and whether translations are spoken aloud or displayed on-screen.

You’re now ready to start the translation.

How to start Live Translation on AirPods

Once setup is complete, Apple gives you several ways to activate Live Translation, so you don’t have to open the Translate app every time.

Method 1: Use the Translate app

  1. Open the Translate app.
  2. Tap Live.
  3. Choose the languages.
  4. Tap Start Translation.

This is probably the easiest method when you first use the feature.

Method 2: Use your AirPods

If you have AirPods 4 with ANC, AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 2, or AirPods Pro 3, press and hold the stems on both AirPods at the same time.

If you’re using AirPods Max 2, press and hold the listening mode button.

Method 3: Ask Siri

You can also say: “Siri, start Live Translation.”

Siri will start the feature when the necessary settings and supported hardware are in place.

Method 4: Use the Action Button

If your compatible iPhone has an Action button, you can configure it to launch Translate.

When you’re wearing your AirPods, using the Action button can automatically start Live Translation.

Method 5: Use Control Center

You can also add Translate to Control Center and use it as a quick way to access Live Translation.

  1. Swipe down from the top-right corner of your iPhone.
  2. Tap Translate.
  3. Start Live Translation.

How to use Live Translation during a conversation

Once Live Translation is running, you don’t have to keep looking at your iPhone.

Simply listen while the other person speaks. Your AirPods will automatically detect the other person’s language, reduce background noise with ANC, and deliver translations directly to your ears.

When it’s your turn to respond:

  1. Speak normally in your language.
  2. Open the Live tab in Translate if you need to show the other person what you’re saying.
  3. Tap the Play button to have your iPhone speak the translated response through its speaker.

If the other person also has compatible AirPods and has started Live Translation, they can hear your translated response through their AirPods. Otherwise, use your iPhone to communicate your response.

Tip: When I’m using Live Translation in a noisy place, I use the iPhone’s microphones to improve the translation input. You may move your iPhone closer to the other person so their speech is captured clearly in addition to the microphones on your AirPods.

Live Translation in Calls

Live Translation isn’t limited to face-to-face conversations.

Apple also supports Live Translation during calls in the Phone app and FaceTime while you’re wearing compatible AirPods.

On an active call:

  1. Start or answer the call normally.
  2. Tap More.
  3. Tap Live Translation.
  4. Choose the language.
  5. Tap Start Translation.

The other person is notified that the call is being translated. As you speak, they hear the translated version, and their response is translated for you. You can also see an on-screen transcription.

Note: Apple warns that Live Translation uses generative models and that translations can sometimes be inaccurate, unexpected, or offensive. For anything important, you should verify the translation rather than treating it as perfect.

How to stop Live Translation

When you’re finished:

  1. Open the Translate app.
  2. Go to the Live tab.
  3. Tap the X button to stop Live Translation.

Tips for the best experience

To get the most accurate translations, keep these in mind:

  • Keep your AirPods and iPhone updated to the latest firmware and iOS version.
  • Use Live Translation in quiet environments for better accuracy.
  • Keep your iPhone nearby, as it handles the translation processing.
  • Speak naturally but clearly. Very fast speech, heavy background noise, or unclear pronunciation can make translation harder.
  • Download language packs before traveling abroad.
  • Ensure your AirPods are fully charged to avoid interruptions.

Breaking language barriers with AirPods

Apple’s Live Translation for AirPods makes global conversations more natural and effortless. Whether you’re traveling, working, or just connecting with someone in a new language, this feature helps you stay focused on the conversation rather than the translation.

Have you tried Live Translation on your AirPods yet? Share your experience in the comments below.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: iOS 27.2 code points to Schneider smart home accessories for Apple Home

content.rendered:
Code in iOS 27.2 reportedly lists two Schneider products as "second-party" Apple Home accessories: a smart thermostat and a temperature and humidity sensor. Developer pdfu posted the findings on X, and 9to5Mac reported the leak. Neither Apple nor Schneider has announced the products, so the code does not confirm a partnership or a launch plan.

The names add Schneider to the companies linked to Apple’s rumored smart home expansion. Separate reporting has described a larger group of accessories developed with LG, but the Schneider clues are limited to two database entries.

The code names two products

The entries are called "Schneider Home Smart Thermostat" and "Schneider Electric Temperature/Humidity Sensor." According to the report, the thermostat is the only one with setup assets in the software. Those graphics are placeholders, and the setup configuration mentions "Proximity Settings." The code does not show what that setting would do or whether it would appear in a finished product.

The label "second-party" appears to distinguish these entries inside Apple’s Home accessory database. 9to5Mac says devices with that designation may receive special treatment from the operating system, but neither the code nor the report explains what that means for people using Apple Home. It does not confirm that Apple designed the products with Schneider, as it reportedly did with LG.

The report leaves basic product details open

There is no public design, price, release date, country list, or compatibility information for the Schneider entries. The names alone do not establish whether they refer to retail products, internal variants, or prototypes. The placeholder thermostat setup graphics also do not reveal how the hardware will look.

The names point to their apparent roles: one could regulate a home’s temperature, while the other measures temperature and humidity. The leak does not say whether they would work together.

The earlier Apple and LG accessory report described a lineup that reportedly includes cameras, a lock, a doorbell, a thermostat, and sensors. The Schneider code mentions only a thermostat and a temperature and humidity sensor. Apple’s rumored screen-equipped Home hub could provide a wider role for compatible accessories, but no connection between the hub and these Schneider entries has been confirmed.

For now, the iOS code is a sign that Apple may be preparing to support more partner accessories in Home. It does not show what Schneider will sell, when it might arrive, or whether the products will be available to consumers at all.

title.rendered: Microsoft offers up to $1,000 for MacBook Pro trade-ins with Surface Laptop Ultra

content.rendered:
Microsoft is offering up to $1,000 in cash back to people who buy a Surface Laptop Ultra and trade in an eligible MacBook Pro. The promotion runs from October 7 to November 23, 2026, through the Microsoft Store online in the U.S. and Canada. The payout depends on the trade-in’s value and inspection, so it is not an automatic $1,000 discount at checkout.

Microsoft opened preorders for the Surface Laptop Ultra at $2,599. The laptop becomes available on October 16. Its official announcement gives the full terms, including the trade-in process and condition requirements.

The trade-in must pass inspection

Buyers must submit an online trade-in claim and proof that they purchased a qualifying new Surface Laptop Ultra during the promotion. They then have 15 days after completing the claim to mail in the MacBook Pro. Teladvance inspects it, and the final cash-back amount varies based on the Surface model and the condition and value of the trade-in.

The MacBook must power on, hold a charge, and be fully functional. Microsoft says it cannot have missing or broken parts, a cracked screen, liquid damage, modifications, or a broken warranty seal. It also cannot be password protected, and the original charger, accessories, and hard drive must be included. If the device fails inspection, it may be returned or recycled, but recycled devices do not qualify for cash back.

The offer is limited to one per customer, cannot be combined with other promotions, and does not apply to previous purchases. Buyers need to complete the online process through Microsoft Store in the U.S. or Canada by November 23. The promotion is not available through retailers that sell the laptop.

The Surface is aimed at demanding workloads

Microsoft positions the Surface Laptop Ultra for creators, developers, and people who want to run AI models locally. The 15-inch touchscreen laptop uses NVIDIA’s RTX Spark platform, with an NVIDIA Blackwell GPU, a Grace CPU, and up to 128GB of unified memory. Microsoft says it can run models with more than 120 billion parameters locally and cites up to one petaflop of AI performance based on theoretical FP4 performance with sparsity.

The laptop also has a broad port selection: three USB-C ports, HDMI, USB-A, an SD card reader, and a 3.5mm headphone jack. One USB-C port supports Microsoft’s built-in magnetic charging connection while remaining available for data and video.

Those specifications help explain why Microsoft is pitching the laptop at people with demanding creative and AI work. They also make the $2,599 starting price a major part of the decision. The trade-in offer may reduce the eventual cost, but buyers still need to pay for the Surface and wait for their MacBook to pass inspection. Anyone weighing that switch against Apple’s current line can compare the 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro or review which MacBook to buy before sending in an older machine.

title.rendered: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 owners report skin irritation

content.rendered:
Some Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 owners say they have felt burning or noticed redness beneath the sensor area. MacRumors reported the complaints from its forums and Reddit, but the posts do not show how common the problem is or what caused it. Apple has not confirmed a sensor-related issue.

The new sensors are one theory

The Series 12 and Ultra 4 use Apple’s latest Health Sensing System. The Series 12 measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day. MacRumors also points to larger green LEDs, a larger ECG electrode surface, and photodiodes arranged in a ring. Owners have wondered whether the redesigned sensor has anything to do with the irritation, but no evidence connects those changes to the reports.

The complaints MacRumors reviewed describe symptoms in the same area where the watch rests against the wrist. Some owners said cleaning the back of the watch or changing the fit helped. Others returned their devices. Those experiences do not confirm a common cause, and similar complaints about Apple Watch have appeared before the current generation.

Fit and moisture can irritate skin

Apple’s wearing guidance says skin reactions can relate to allergies or sensitivity to materials, sweat or soap trapped against the skin, and a band that is too tight or too loose. Apple says a small number of people may react to nickel or trace acrylates and methacrylates in some cases, though the latter are designed to stay out of direct skin contact. A tight band can irritate the skin, while a loose one can rub. Apple recommends keeping the watch, band, and skin clean and dry, especially after workouts or contact with liquids such as sweat, soap, sunscreen, or lotion.

That guidance does not explain the new reports. It does show why redness under a watch cannot, by itself, identify a defect in the sensor. The Apple Watch Ultra 4’s health features and other Apple Watch health tools rely on close contact with the wrist, but Apple’s advice also accounts for fit and skin sensitivity.

What owners should do

Apple says people who notice redness, swelling, itchiness, or other irritation should consult a physician before wearing the watch again. Its guidance also recommends checking the fit and cleaning the watch and band, particularly after exercise. Owners in the reports tried some of those steps, but the anecdotes are not enough to show whether they address a sensor problem.

title.rendered: My Anime Mine codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest My Anime Mine Codes on October 12, 2026

My Anime Mine brings you both mining and your favorite anime characters in a unique Roblox game. In this game, you’ll mine rocks to discover new characters and ores, build your crew, and sell your resources to keep your mining operation running. As you progress, you will be able to upgrade your crew and make them powerful, but you’ll need resources like Strength Dice, Mutation Luck, and Enchanted Dice to do so.

Unfortunately, getting your hands on these resources isn’t easy. However, My Anime Mine codes can help you stock up on these freebies and make your progression easier. So, let’s take a look at the complete list of codes you can redeem right now.

All working My Anime Mine codes

  • MOONRISE: 1 Enchanted Dice (NEW)
  • HALLOWKEEP: 2 Enchanted Dice (NEW)
  • BLUEMOON: 1 Enchanted Dice and 1 Ore Elixir II (NEW)
  • SOULFORGE: 1 Enchanted Dice and 1 Summon Scroll
  • EnchantedStrength: 1 Strength Potion and 1 Enchanted Dice
  • MUTATIONLUCK: 1 Mutation Luck Potion I
  • LifeIsRoblox NEW: 2 Enchanted Dice

As of now, these are the only active My Anime Mine codes available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired or unverified My Anime Mine codes

CODEMADNESS, ENCHANTED, ENCHANTEDFIRST100, ENCHANTEDFIRST50, ENCHANTEDSUMMONS

How to redeem My Anime Mine codes

Now that you know all the active codes, it’s also crucial to know how to redeem them. Luckily, the process is quite simple and only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem My Anime Mine codes:

  1. Fire up My Anime Mine on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on the Gift Codes button from the menu on the right side of the screen.
  4. Paste a working code and click Confirm to claim your reward.
  5. Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Where to find more My Anime Mine codes

The developers don’t release new My Anime Mine codes on a fixed schedule. Most new codes appear alongside major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official My Anime Mine Discord server for announcements.
  • Follow the game’s Roblox page for update notifications.
  • Bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated whenever new codes are released.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Meow Madness codes, Blue Lock Farm codes and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

Why are My Anime Mine codes not working?

Make sure you’ve entered the code exactly as it’s displayed in the list above. If it still doesn’t work, there’s a chance the code has expired or already been redeemed.

What do My Anime Mine codes do?

My Anime Mine codes give free rewards such as Enchanted Dice, Summon Scrolls, Strength Potions, and Mutation Luck boosts. These rewards can help with game progression.

title.rendered: FNAF Bonnie locations in Fortnite: Where to find and beat him

content.rendered:
Bonnie the Rabbit, one of the most popular characters from Five Nights at Freddy’s, has arrived in Fortnite Override as both an in-game boss and a playable skin. Other FNAF animatronics, including Freddy, Chica, and Roxy, have also joined the game as part of the crossover.

Unlike Freddy and Roxy, Bonnie is one of two bosses, alongside Chica, who doesn’t appear at Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria on the Fortnite map. Instead, Bonnie can randomly spawn at several locations across the island. Here’s where you should look.

FNAF Bonnie boss fight locations in Fortnite

Bonnie the Rabbit can spawn at several Fortnite map locations. However, his spawn is randomized each match, so you’re not guaranteed to find him at a particular POI.

If Bonnie isn’t at your chosen location, you may need to check another spawn point or try again in a new match.

Chopped Shop: Head to the largest building in the northwestern part of the area. Bonnie can spawn inside or around this building.

Golden Grove: There are two possible Bonnie spawn locations here. The first is near the car wash in the southwestern part of the area, while the second is close to the large building on the eastern side.

Lifty Lodge: Search the buildings in the northeastern section of the neighborhood to find Bonnie the Rabbit.

Shaken Sanctuary: Bonnie can also spawn around the structure in the northwestern section of Shaken Sanctuary.

Since Bonnie can appear at different locations in each match, it’s worth choosing a landing spot where you can quickly loot weapons before checking his spawn point.

How to defeat FNAF Bonnie in Fortnite

Truthfully, searching for Bonnie is more difficult than the actual boss fight with the awe-inspiring animatronic. When you find him at a spawn point, he won’t attack until you close in the distance. Once you do that, he will only stalk you on foot and not do any swift maneuvers like certain other bosses, such as Adam Smasher, do. So, you can conveniently retreat when required in the middle of a fight.

Moreover, Bonnie will only attack you with a pickaxe and nothing else, so the damage dealt by him is also not too bad. On the other hand, taking Bonnie down isn’t a big assignment either, as you can do that with something as easily obtainable as an Uncommon-tier 8-Bit Shotgun.

Successfully defeating Bonnie the Rabbit unlocks three different major rewards. Firstly, you get a Mythic-tier High Stakes’ Shotgun and a Legendary Chug Jug. Alongside that, you also get the option of playing as the defeated boss himself by using the “Possess” option.

This way you can not just trial run the Bonnie skin, which is available on the Item Shop at the time of writing, but can also earn something of a one-up life. That’s because, if you are downed while Bonnie is in your possession, you will respawn as your original character with some health and all your weapons intact.

Wrapping up

Based on the fact that FNAF boss fights, including the one versus Bonnie, are easy to beat and that their rewards are very effective, it would be a smart decision to complete this encounter in the early stages of a Fortnite match, so that you can maximize the use of the valuable loot in the most important circumstances later. You may even do it in as many matches as you want.

After Fortnite bosses from Pac-Man, Sonic The Hedgehog, Cyberpunk 2077, and FNAF landing in the online title, it will be interesting to see which other video game characters are enrolled into the season as an adversary next. With under four weeks left in Fortnite Override, it’s safe to say that we will find out more on that front in the near future.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • How to get Jimothy the Raccoon sidekick for free in Fortnite
  • How to get Vampire Sprite in Fortnite
  • Flusher in Fortnite: What it is and where to find it
  • Jack the Clown arrives in Fortnite: Here’s how to get the skin

title.rendered: Jack the Clown arrives in Fortnite: Here’s how to get the skin

content.rendered:
Jack Schmidt, aka Jack the Clown, has landed in Fortnite as part of the latest lineup of Item Shop cosmetics. This marks the debut of the Halloween Horror Nights character in the game, joining other newcomers this month, such as Freddy Fazbear from Five Nights at Freddy’s and Freddy Krueger from A Nightmare on Elm Street.

The Jack the Clown skin and its related cosmetics are available individually or as part of the Jack the Clown Bundle. While the skin alone costs 1,500 V-Bucks, the complete bundle is available at a discounted price of 2,000 V-Bucks. All these items are available only until October 12 at 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET.

How to claim Jack the Clown skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Halloween Horror Nights section (under Fortnitemares) and select Jack the Clown skin.
  3. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

When you purchase the Jack the Clown skin, you also get the Jack the Clown in the Box back bling at no additional cost. The back bling is also available separately in the Shop for players who only want that particular item.

All Jack the Clown cosmetics in Fortnite

Jack the Clown

  • Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
  • Also includes: Jack the Clown in the Box back bling
  • Also available with: Jack the Clown Bundle

Jack the Clown in the Box back bling

  • Price: 400 V-Bucks
  • Also available with: Jack the Clown Bundle

Jack’s Menacing Mallet pickaxe

  • Price: 800 V-Bucks
  • Also available with: Jack the Clown Bundle

Chainsaw Balloon emote

  • Price: 300 V-Bucks
  • Also available with: Jack the Clown Bundle

Apart from Jack the Clown-inspired items, several cosmetics based on other popular franchises are also available at the time of writing. These include items from A Nightmare on Elm Street, Black Clover, and Five Nights at Freddy’s.

Final thoughts

Throughout October, the Fortnitemares event is setting the mood for the Halloween season with several major collaborations that have either already arrived or are coming soon. The arrival of Jack the Clown is the latest addition to this year’s celebrations.

Fortnitemares isn’t limited to horror-themed cosmetics, either. The event also brings gameplay changes, Battle Royale map updates, and other spooky additions. New Sprites, such as the Vampire Sprite and Spooky Dash Sprite, are among the notable additions this year. As October progresses, we can expect even more Fortnitemares content to arrive in Fortnite.

FAQs

Who is Jack the Clown?

Jack the Clown is an iconic character from Universal’s Halloween Horror Nights. The character first appeared at Halloween Horror Nights in 2000.

Can I get the Jack the Clown skin for free in Fortnite?

title.rendered: All Pumpkin Chest locations in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4

content.rendered:
Fortnitemares is in full swing in Fortnite, bringing not only exciting crossovers but also plenty of spooky items to discover across the island. One of these is the Pumpkin Chest, a limited-time chest that can reward you with powerful weapons, Sprites, and other useful loot.

However, tracking down Pumpkin Chests isn’t always easy, especially with so much happening across the island during Fortnitemares. To make your search easier, we’ve put together a complete guide covering all Pumpkin Chest locations in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4, along with the rewards you can get from opening them.

All Pumpkin Chest locations in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4

There are a total of 45 Pumpkin Chests scattered across the Fortnite island during Fortnitemares 2026. If you want to find several without traveling too far, some of the best areas to search are north of Stone Sanctum, Wonkeeland, and Nightmare Neighborhood.

Fortunately, Pumpkin Chests are fairly easy to recognize once you’re nearby. They have a distinctive purple glow and a large, creepy Jack-o’-lantern face, making them stand out from regular chests.

You can use the map below to find all 45 Pumpkin Chest locations in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4.

Since other players may also be hunting for these chests, consider landing near an area with multiple Pumpkin Chest spawns. This gives you a better chance of opening one before another player gets there.

What do Pumpkin Chests do in Fortnite?

Now that you know where to find Pumpkin Chests, you might be wondering whether they’re actually worth searching for. The short answer is yes, especially if you’re looking for powerful loot or specific Sprites.

Each Pumpkin Chest contains randomized loot, with a chance to drop Legendary weapons and other useful gear. However, the biggest reason to open one is the guaranteed Sprite.

Depending on the chest, you can get Sprites such as:

  • Bounty Hunter Sprite
  • Morgana Sprite
  • Blinky Sprite
  • Vampire Sprite

Fortnitemares 2026 introduced several Halloween-themed Sprites, including the Vampire Sprite, which can also be obtained from Pumpkin Chests.

Opening Pumpkin Chests can also contribute toward certain Fortnitemares quests, giving you another reason to track them down while exploring the island.

How to open a Pumpkin Chest in Fortnite

Opening a Pumpkin Chest works just like opening most other containers in Fortnite. Simply walk up to the chest and hold the Interact button until it opens.

On PC, the default interact key is F, while controller players can use their assigned interact button. Once opened, the Pumpkin Chest will drop its Sprite along with any weapons and other loot inside.

Just make sure the area is clear before opening one. The chest-opening animation leaves you vulnerable for a moment, and popular Pumpkin Chest locations can attract other players looking for the same loot.

Are Pumpkin Chests worth opening?

Yes. Pumpkin Chests are particularly useful during Fortnitemares because you’re getting more than the usual random chest loot. The guaranteed Sprite alone makes them worth seeking out, while the chance of getting high-rarity weapons can give you an advantage early in a match.

If you’re already near one of the 45 locations, there’s little reason to pass one up.

Final thoughts

title.rendered: How to customize your iPhone’s Photos app

content.rendered:
The Photos app went through one of its biggest redesigns with iOS 18, replacing the familiar tab-based interface with a unified, scrollable layout. Apple later refined that approach based on user feedback, and the Photos app in iOS 27 continues with separate Library and Collections tabs while giving users considerably more control over how their photos are organized.

I find the customization options particularly useful because the default Collections view can put Apple’s automatically generated collections ahead of the albums and sections I actually use. In iOS 27, you can change the size and appearance of collection tiles, reorder collections, customize Pinned Collections, and control how people and pets are featured.

Here’s how to customize the Photos app on your iPhone running iOS 27.

Table of Contents
  • How to customize the Photos app view on iPhone
  • How to sort and filter your Photo Library
    • Apply filters to your Library
  • How to hide screenshots and shared photos from your Library
  • How to hide or reduce photos of someone in People & Pets
  • How to modify pinned collections in the Photos app
  • How to remove photos from Featured Photos
  • How to customize albums
  • How to reorder Items in the Media Types and Utilities Collections
  • How to disable the recently viewed & Shared Collections under Utilities
  • Signing off…

How to customize the Photos app view on iPhone

Apple redesigned the Photos app to make navigation easier. However, the redesign focuses more on system-generated albums than what a user would want. Fortunately, Apple has prepared in advance for this situation and allows you to customize the default Photos app view to suit your fancy.

Here’s how to customize the Collections view:

  1. Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Collections at the bottom.
  3. Tap the three-dot button at the top of the screen.
  4. Choose one of the available display options:
    • Large Grid to make collection tiles larger.
    • Small Grid to make them smaller.
    • Mixed Grid to return to the default mixed layout.
    • Collapse All to hide the collection image tiles.
  5. If you want to change the order of your collections, tap Reorder.
  6. Touch and hold a collection and drag it to your preferred position.
  7. Once you’re satisfied with the changes you’ve made, tap the Right Tick (Done) button in the top right corner.

Apple also lets you choose which library is represented in Collections if you use an iCloud Shared Photo Library. You can choose Both Libraries, Personal Library, or Shared Library.

My tip: I prefer keeping the collections I use most frequently near the top. If you mainly use Photos for albums rather than automatically generated memories, moving Albums and other frequently used collections higher up can make the app much quicker to navigate.

How to sort and filter your Photo Library

iOS 27 also gives you better control over the main photo library itself.

You can sort photos by when they were added to your library or when they were originally captured.

  1. Open Photos.
  2. Go to your Library.
  3. Tap the Sort and Filter button at the top.
  4. Choose Added or Captured.

The Added option organizes photos according to when they were added to your library, while Captured sorts them according to when they were taken.

Apply filters to your Library

You can also filter the library instead of scrolling through everything.

  1. Open Photos.
  2. Tap the Sort and Filter button.
  3. Choose a filter such as:
    • Edited
    • Favorites
    • Shared with You
    • Captured by Me
    • Media Types

You can combine multiple filters, which is useful when you’re trying to find a specific type of photo. For example, I can use Media Types to show only videos, screenshots, or photos and combine that with another filter.

To return to the complete library, tap Remove Filters.

How to hide screenshots and shared photos from your Library

If your photo library is full of screenshots, photos synced from a Mac, or images shared with you through Messages, iOS 27 lets you hide those categories from the main library without deleting them.

Here’s how:

  1. Open Photos.
  2. Tap the Sort and Filter button.
  3. Tap View Options.
  4. Choose the type of content you want to hide:
    • Screenshots
    • From My Mac
    • Shared with You

Tap the option again if you want those items to appear in your library again.

This is one of the changes I’d recommend trying if your Library feels unnecessarily cluttered.

How to hide or reduce photos of someone in People & Pets

The People & Pets collection automatically groups photos based on the people and animals Photos recognizes in your library. You can click on any Headshot to view a collection of images featuring that individual.

However, you don’t have to let Photos repeatedly feature someone you don’t want appearing in Memories, Featured Photos, or other curated areas. The controls also let you create a group of two or more individuals, or even add new individuals to the People and Pets section.

Here’s how:

  1. Open the Photos app and move to the Collections screen. 
  2. Here, scroll down and tap People. 
  3. Now, tap Edit in the top-right corner and select the People you want to hide.
  4. Once done, tap the three-dot button in the bottom-right corner, then tap Hide in the pop-up menu.
  5. Next, tap Hide from People Album in the confirmation prompt.
  6. Alternatively, you can tap Create New Group so that the photos of the selected individuals will appear in a single album.
  7. To add new People to the People and Pets section, tap the “+” button in the top-right corner.  
  8. Next, select People from the available options, then tap the Right Tick (Done) button in the top-right corner.

You can further customize the People album to change someone’s key photo, merge groups of the same person, or stop featuring some people.

How to modify pinned collections in the Photos app

By default, the Pinned Collections in the Photos app comprise the albums iOS thinks are most important to you, but this may only hold true for some users. If you are not one of those users, you can modify the Pinned Collections at your convenience.

  1. With the Photos app open, move to the Collections screen. 
  2. Here, scroll down and tap the Edit button next to Pinned Collection. 
  3. Here, tap the – button before an album and select Delete to remove it from the Pinned Collection. 
  4. Alternatively, tap the + button before an album to add it to the Pinned Collection. 
  5. Additionally, scroll down to the bottom and tap Add Collection or Album to add something other than the suggested collection.
  6. To change the order, touch and hold a pinned collection and drag it to a new position.
  7. Tap the Close button when you’re finished.

There’s also a quicker way to manage this. You can touch and hold a collection or album and select Pin to add it to Pinned, or select Unpin to remove it.

How to remove photos from Featured Photos

The Featured Photos section includes images from various years featuring you and different people your iPhone selected to highlight. However, not all memories are worth celebrating.

So, keeping that in mind, the Photos app allows you to remove photos from the Featured Photos album.

Here’s how:

  1. Open the Photos app and tap the Collections tab at the bottom.
  2. Here, scroll down and tap on Featured Photos.
  3. Next, tap the Select button in the top-right corner and select the photos you want to remove from this collection.
  4. Once done, tap the three-dot button at the top.
  5. Now, tap Remove from Featured Photos in the contextual menu.

How to customize albums

Albums remain available under Collections, and iOS 27 gives you additional ways to organize them.

To create an album:

  1. Go to Collections in the Photos app.
  2. Tap Albums.
  3. Tap the Add (+) button.
  4. Choose New Album.
  5. Enter an album name.
  6. Tap Add Photos to select the photos you want to add.
  7. Tap the checkmark to save it.

You can also sort albums by different options, including a custom order. With Sort by Custom Order selected, touch and hold an album, then drag it to the position you want. You can also drag an album onto another to merge them.

How to reorder Items in the Media Types and Utilities Collections

If the default view of the Media Types or Utilities collections feels off to you, you can reorder the items according to your will. However, your iPhone must be running iOS 18 or later to do so. Here’s how:

  1. Move to the Collections tab in the Photos app.
  2. Scroll down and tap Media Types or Utilities.
  3. Here, tap the Edit button at the top right corner.
  4. Now, drag and drop an item to change its position.
  5. Once satisfied, tap the Right Tick (Done) button at the top right corner.

How to disable the recently viewed & Shared Collections under Utilities

While most of the collections under Utilities deserve their spot, the same can’t be said about the Recently Viewed and Recently Shared collections. On iOS 18.4 and later, you can disable Recently Viewed and Recently Shared in Photos settings. Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings, scroll down, and tap on Apps.
  2. Here, locate and tap on Photos.
  3. Now, scroll down and select Albums.
  4. Toggle off Show Recently Viewed & Shared.

From here, you can go to Featured Content to stop Memories and holiday events from automatically appearing on your device.

Signing off…

The Photos app has come a long way since the controversial redesign introduced with iOS 18. Rather than simply restoring the old interface, Apple has continued refining the Library and Collections approach while giving users more control over how the app is organized.

In iOS 27, I find the Layout and Reorder controls particularly useful because they let me decide how much space Collections occupy and which sections appear first. Pinned Collections also make it easier to keep my most-used albums and collections within quick reach.

If the default Photos layout doesn’t work for you, I wouldn’t simply put up with it. Spend a few minutes customizing Collections, Pinned items, People & Pets, and Library filters, and the Photos app can feel much more personal and considerably easier to navigate.

@graph.name: How to Customize the Photos App View on iPhone
@graph.description: Personalize your Photos app home screen by rearranging, replacing, or removing collections and albums on your iPhone.

step.name: Open customization options
step.text: Open the Photos app, scroll to the bottom, and tap Customize & Reorder.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Photos app on your iPhone.
Scroll to the bottom and tap Customize & Reorder.

step.name: Replace an album tile
step.text: Tap the Replace button under any Album tile to change it to a different collection.

itemListElement.text: Tap Replace under the tile you want to change.
Select a new collection to display in its place.

step.name: Reorder album tiles
step.text: Tap and hold any Collection, then drag and drop it to a new position.

itemListElement.text: Tap, hold, and drag a Collection tile to rearrange its order.

step.name: Remove a collection from home screen
step.text: Uncheck any collection you no longer want to appear on the Photos app home screen.

itemListElement.text: Uncheck the box next to any collection to hide it.

step.name: Exit or reset customization
step.text: Tap the X at the top right to exit customization. Or, tap Reset at the top left to revert to default layout.

itemListElement.text: Tap X at the top right to save and exit.
Tap Reset to restore the original layout if needed.

@graph.name: How to Hide People in the People & Pets Section
@graph.description: Easily remove or hide specific individuals from the People & Pets section in your iPhone's Photos app.

step.name: Open the People section
step.text: Open the Photos app, scroll down, and tap on the People section.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
Scroll down and tap People.

step.name: Select individuals to hide
step.text: Choose the people you want to hide from the People album.

itemListElement.text: Tap on the faces you want to hide.

step.name: Hide selected people
step.text: Tap the three-dot button at the bottom right corner, then select Hide. Confirm by tapping Remove from People Album.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three-dot menu at the bottom right.
Select Hide from the menu.
Tap Remove from People Album to confirm.

step.name: Optional: Create a new group
step.text: You can also create a custom group with selected individuals for easier access.

itemListElement.text: Tap Create New Group at the bottom.
Select the people to include and tap Add.

step.name: Optional: Add more people
step.text: To add someone to the People & Pets section, tap Add People and select from available faces.

itemListElement.text: Tap Add People at the bottom of the People screen.
Select individuals and tap Add in the top-right corner.

@graph.name: How to Modify Pinned Collections in the Photos App
@graph.description: Learn how to customize the Pinned Collection in the Photos app by adding, removing, or creating albums for quick access.

step.name: Open the Pinned Collection
step.text: With the Photos app open, scroll down to the Pinned Collection and tap the Modify button.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
Scroll down to find the Pinned Collection section.
Tap the Modify button to begin editing.

step.name: Remove albums from the Pinned Collection
step.text: Tap the minus button before an album to remove it from the Pinned Collection.

itemListElement.text: Look for the album you want to remove.
Tap the minus button beside it.

step.name: Add albums to the Pinned Collection
step.text: Tap the plus button before an album to add it to the Pinned Collection.

itemListElement.text: Browse through the available albums.
Tap the plus button beside the album you want to pin.

step.name: Add a new collection or album
step.text: Tap the Add Collection or Album button if you want to add something other than the suggested collections.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Add Collection or Album button at the bottom of the screen.
Choose the album or collection you want to include.

@graph.name: How to Remove Photos from Featured Photos
@graph.description: Easily remove unwanted pictures from Featured Photos in the Photos app to keep your highlights more personalized.

step.name: Open Featured Photos
step.text: With the Photos app open, scroll down and tap on Featured Photos.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
Scroll down until you see Featured Photos.
Tap Featured Photos to view the collection.

step.name: Select the photos you want to remove
step.text: Tap the Select button, then choose the photos you want to remove from Featured Photos.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Select button at the top.
Tap on each photo you want to remove.

step.name: Remove from Featured Photos
step.text: Once done, tap the three dot button at the bottom right corner, then select Remove from Featured Photos.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three dot button at the bottom right corner.
Choose Remove from Featured Photos from the menu.

keyPoints.title: iOS 18 Photos App Redesign Reversed in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Apple brought back the classic tab-based structure in the Photos app after user feedback, replacing the system that focused more on system-generated albums.

keyPoints.title: Customizing the Photos App View in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Users can now reorder collections in the Photos app by entering editing mode in the Collections tab, allowing a more personalized navigation.

keyPoints.title: How to Hide People & Pets in the Photos App
keyPoints.explanation: You can hide specific individuals in the People & Pets section by selecting them and choosing 'Hide', or create new groups for better organization.

keyPoints.title: Modify Pinned Collections for Better Access
keyPoints.explanation: The default pinned collections can be customized by adding or removing albums through the edit options in the Collections tab.

keyPoints.title: Removing Unwanted Photos from Featured Photos
keyPoints.explanation: You can select and remove specific photos from the Featured Photos section, helping curate your favorite memories more easily.

title.rendered: iPhone wallpaper dimensions and sizes: complete guide for all models

content.rendered:
Use your iPhone’s screen resolution as a starting point when choosing a wallpaper. Matching the screen’s shape helps avoid awkward crops; using a larger image keeps it sharp when you zoom in.

If you are not sure which iPhone you have, find the model name and number first.

Why wallpaper dimensions matter

An image with the wrong shape may lose its edges when iOS fills the screen. A file smaller than the display can also look soft after you enlarge it. The chart below groups models that share a resolution, so you can choose the right size without sorting through every launch year.

iPhone screen sizes and resolutions

These are portrait display resolutions. Aspect ratios are approximate; iOS may crop the image slightly when you set it.

Choose a wallpaper that stays sharp

For the sharpest result, use a portrait image at your iPhone’s native resolution or larger, with a similar aspect ratio. There is no universal extra-pixel rule: a larger file gives you more room to zoom, but a close ratio matters just as much because iOS crops the image to fill the screen.

If your image is smaller than the display, it may look blurry when enlarged. If it is much wider or taller, iOS will trim the excess. Keep faces, text, and logos away from the edges so the crop does not cut them off.

Portrait or landscape wallpapers

Portrait images fit an iPhone screen with less cropping. A landscape photo can still work, but iOS must enlarge and crop it to fill the tall display. Choose one with open space around the subject, or use a portrait version if you want to keep the whole scene.

Design a wallpaper that works on the Lock Screen

Keep the main subject clear of the top-centre camera cutout and leave room for the clock and widgets. Their position can vary with your Lock Screen setup, so check the preview before saving. For a Home Screen wallpaper, avoid placing important details where app icons will cover them.

How to set a wallpaper on iPhone

On current iOS, add the image from Settings:

  1. Open Settings and tap Wallpaper.
  2. Tap Add New Wallpaper, then choose Photos.
  3. Select the image and adjust its position.
  4. Tap Add, then choose Set as Wallpaper Pair or Customise Home Screen.

If the image is already open in Photos, the Share menu is a shortcut to the same wallpaper preview:

  1. Open the Photos app and choose the image you want to set as wallpaper.
  2. Tap Share → Use as Wallpaper.
  3. Pinch to zoom or adjust framing.
  4. Tap Add, then choose Set as Wallpaper Pair or Customise Home Screen.

Find an iPhone wallpaper

Browse aesthetic, minimalist, and Dynamic Island wallpapers for designs made around the iPhone’s tall screen. Use the largest download available for your model, then check the Lock Screen preview before applying it.

For most iPhones, matching the portrait shape and keeping the file at or above the screen resolution is enough. Adjust the crop only if the preview cuts off something you want to keep.

  • How to take a screenshot on an iPhone and iPad

title.rendered: Apple schedules Q4 2026 earnings report for November 2

content.rendered:
Apple will report its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results on Monday, November 2. The company’s Investor Relations calendar lists the results for 1:30 p.m. Pacific, followed by a 2 p.m. conference call with CEO John Ternus and CFO Kevan Parekh.

It will be Ternus’s first earnings call as CEO. Apple announced that he took over the role from Tim Cook on September 1.

The quarter includes launch-week iPhone 18 Pro sales

Apple’s fiscal Q4 ran from June 28 through September 26. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max went on sale September 18, so the results will include the first nine days of sales for the new models. Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, and AirPods 5 also launched that day.

The iPhone Duo will not appear in the Q4 numbers. Apple says the device goes on sale October 23, nearly a month after the quarter closed. Its sales will be part of the following quarter instead.

Apple’s July outlook sets a benchmark

During its July earnings call, Apple said it expected total revenue for the September quarter to grow 9% to 11% year over year. The company also expected iPhone revenue to grow in the mid-teens, while noting foreign-exchange headwinds and tighter supply for iPhone, Mac, and iPad.

Apple reported $102.5 billion in Q4 2025 revenue. Applying the July growth range to that figure points to about $111.7 billion to $113.7 billion for this quarter. That is a calculation from Apple’s prior-year revenue and guidance, not a new forecast. The previous Q4 results provide the year-over-year baseline.

Apple also forecast a 47% to 48% gross margin for the September quarter. That is below the 50.1% reported for June, although tariff refunds added about two percentage points to the June figure. Apple’s June-quarter revenue grew 16%, but September brought higher memory costs and price increases across parts of the lineup.

The November 2 call will be Ternus’s first earnings call as CEO. July’s earnings call included CFO Kevan Parekh’s comments on slower Services growth.

mainEntity.name: Who is Jack the Clown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Jack the Clown is an iconic character from Universal's Halloween Horror Nights. The character first appeared at Halloween Horror Nights in 2000.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the Jack the Clown skin for free in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The Jack the Clown skin isn't available for free. You can purchase it from the Fortnite Item Shop for 1,500 V-Bucks.

mainEntity.name: Which Other Horror Characters Can I Buy From the Fortnite Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, other horror characters available in the Item Shop include Ghost Face, Freddy Fazbear, Chica the Chicken, Foxy the Pirate, Bonnie the Rabbit, and Ash Williams from Evil Dead.
