title.rendered: I tried Write With Siri on iOS 27 to rewrite my messages: Here’s what happened

content.rendered:
I write a lot of messages every day, and often end up rewriting them before hitting send. Sometimes a message is too long, the wording feels awkward, or I just can’t find the right tone.

That’s why I was curious about Write With Siri in iOS 27. Apple says Siri can now help write, rewrite, proofread, and improve text using Apple Intelligence. But does it actually make everyday messages better without making them sound like they were written by AI?

What is Write With Siri in iOS 27?

Write With Siri is part of Apple’s next-generation Apple Intelligence features in iOS 27. It lets you use Siri AI to compose, rewrite, proofread, edit, and get feedback on text without leaving the app where you’re writing.

In practice, that means I can be inside Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, or a supported third-party app and ask Siri to generate text from scratch based on a natural-language request. It can also work with text I’ve already written and modify it based on instructions such as making it more formal, friendly, concise, or polished.

More interestingly, Apple says Siri can reflect how you normally communicate with a particular person, including your usual punctuation and tone in Mail and Messages.

My first test: Asking Siri AI to write a message

My first test was deliberately simple. Instead of writing a message myself, I asked Siri AI to create one from scratch.

The workflow is surprisingly straightforward. When the writing field is active in a supported app, you can see the Write With Siri button above your keyboard. Tap it to type your prompt or use the microphone to tell Siri your request. Then hit the search button in the keyboard.

I tried vague prompts like asking Siri to write a short thank-you message. The first thing I noticed was how little I needed to specify. It doesn’t need a perfect prompt such as: “Generate a warm but concise thank-you message with a conversational tone.” You can simply describe what you want in normal language.

The generated message was polished, grammatically clean, and usable. But there was one catch. And that became a recurring theme during my testing.

For a professional email or an important message, that’s useful. For a casual text to someone I know well, I sometimes found myself removing the polished wording because it sounded more formal than I would naturally type.

Rewrite existing text with Siri AI

This is where Write With Siri became much more useful.

Writing something from scratch is nice, but there are already plenty of AI tools that can do that. The feature became interesting when I started writing messages myself and then asking Siri AI to improve them.

For example, I’d type a rough message with missing punctuation, awkward wording, or a sentence that was much longer than it needed to be.

Instead of deleting it and starting again, I could ask Siri to rewrite it.

To do so:

  1. Write or select the text.
  2. Tap the Siri AI icon on the floating menu.
  3. Now, you can tell Siri what changes you want.
  4. Review the rewritten version.
  5. Keep it, modify it again using the Edit with Siri option, or return to the original by tapping the undo button.

Furthermore, Apple offers a Compare option that allows me to review the original and rewritten versions rather than blindly accepting the AI-generated text.

I also tested different instructions:

  • “Make this shorter.”
  • “Make this more friendly.”
  • “Make this sound professional.”
  • “Make this less formal.”
  • “Fix the grammar.”
  • “Make this clearer.”
  • “Expand this slightly.”

The results were generally predictable. The shorter version actually became shorter. The formal version sounded more professional. The proofreading request focused on grammar rather than completely rewriting everything.

That sounds basic, but it makes a difference when I’m already happy with what I wrote and only want one specific thing changed.

Does Write With Siri actually preserve my voice?

This was the test I cared about most.

AI can fix grammar all day long, but if the result sounds nothing like me, I probably won’t use it for personal messages.

Apple says Siri AI can match a user’s writing style, punctuation, and tone in Messages and Mail, including adapting to the way they communicate with individual recipients.

In my testing, I found that the idea works better when I give Siri something to work with. If I ask Siri to create a message from scratch, the result can feel like a generic AI-written message.

But when I give it my own rough text and ask for a rewrite, the result feels much closer to my original intent.

Other useful Write With Siri features

The more I used Write With Siri, the more I realized that rewriting a message is only one small part of what Apple’s AI writing assistant can actually do.

What makes it interesting in iOS 27 is that Write With Siri works systemwide wherever you type. So you’re not limited to Messages. You can use it while writing emails, notes, documents, and other supported text fields without having to jump into a separate AI app.

Automatic proofreading while I type

iOS 27 adds automatic proofreading for spelling and grammar while typing in apps. The system can catch common writing problems as I’m composing text.

For someone who types quickly, this is arguably more useful than having to stop, select everything, and ask an AI to proofread it afterward.

Ask Siri how my writing sounds

Instead of simply asking Siri to rewrite your text, you can select something you’ve written and select the “How does this sound?” option. That turns Siri into something closer to a writing editor. You can even ask the following questions to make your writing comprehensive.

For example, if I’m writing a presentation or an important email, I can ask for feedback rather than immediately replacing my words. This approach is ideal when you don’t want AI to rewrite your work.

Edit text using natural-language instructions

This is probably my favorite part of Write With Siri.

Instead of manually editing a paragraph, I can simply select the text and describe the change I want.

For example:

  • “Make this email sound more formal.”
  • “Rewrite this to be friendlier.”
  • “Shorten this to three sentences.”
  • “Turn these bullet points into a paragraph.”
  • “Make this easier to understand.”

If the existing text was written by Siri AI, you will see a Rewrite option when you select the text. It will give you a different version. If it’s still not good enough, tap the Edit with Siri button and describe your changes.

Turn rough notes into proper writing

Another useful trick is taking fragmented thoughts and turning them into something readable.

For example, you might have several bullet points that make sense to you but aren’t ready to send to someone. Instead of rewriting each point manually, you can ask Siri to turn the bullet points into a paragraph.

This could be particularly useful for:

  • Work notes
  • Meeting summaries
  • Emails
  • Project updates
  • Personal notes
  • Presentation content

It’s a small feature, but it’s exactly the sort of repetitive writing task where AI can save time.

Shorten without starting over

I also found myself using Siri when something I had written was simply too long.

Rather than deleting half the paragraph myself, I can tell Siri to shorten it.

The best part is you can ask it to reduce something to a particular number of sentences or make it more concise while keeping the important information.

The bigger advantage: I don’t have to leave what I’m doing

I’ve used plenty of AI writing tools before. The problem isn’t usually whether they can rewrite something.

The problem is friction. Normally, the process looks something like this:

Select text → copy → open AI app → paste → write prompt → copy result → return to original app → paste again.

Write With Siri cuts out most of those steps.

You can stay inside the app where you’re already writing and ask Siri to handle the change. That’s what makes this feel less like another AI chatbot and more like an actual iPhone writing feature.

When I’d actually use Write With Siri

After testing it, I don’t think Write With Siri is needed for every message. That would actually defeat the point. If I’m texting a friend: “Where are you?” I don’t need AI.

But there are plenty of situations where I’d happily use it.

  • Important messages: If you’re sending something where wording matters, use Siri AI to check it. A quick rewrite can make an important message clearer.
  • Work emails: When you know what you want to say but the wording feels messy, asking Siri to make it more professional or concise is much faster than starting again.
  • Messages written in a hurry: We’ve all sent messages that were basically one long sentence with no punctuation. Instead of fixing it manually, I can ask Siri to clean it up.
  • When English isn’t coming naturally: Sometimes finding the right English phrasing takes longer than it should. Write With Siri can bridge that gap.

When I wouldn’t use it

There are also plenty of situations where I wouldn’t bother.

  • Casual conversations: Overly polished messages can make conversations with friends and family feel strange.
  • Very short messages: If your message is only one or two sentences, rewriting it with AI can take longer than simply fixing it yourself.
  • Messages where my exact wording matters: AI rewriting can change emphasis, personality, or nuance even when the grammar becomes better.
  • When the original already sounds good: If my message is saying exactly what I want it to say, there’s no need for any optimization.

One thing that still bothered me about Write With Siri

The concept is excellent, but the first version of the feature isn’t completely frictionless.

While testing, I found several early issues in iOS 27. Sometimes, the writing interface disappeared after taking a screenshot, comparison screens became awkward to exit, and the keyboard or interface occasionally vanished while rewriting.

I also think Apple’s decision to make Write With Siri so prominent while typing may not appeal to everyone. Let’s hope Apple improves the experience through next iOS 27 updates.

Final take: Did Write With Siri improve my messages?

Yes, but not in the way I initially expected.

I don’t think Write With Siri is going to replace dedicated AI writing tools for serious writing. What makes it interesting is how quickly it handles the small writing problems I encounter throughout the day.

A message that’s too long, an email that’s too formal, a sentence with terrible grammar, a thought that makes sense in my head but looks terrible when I type it. Those are exactly the moments where Write With Siri makes sense.

Will you use Write With Siri? Let me know in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

mainEntity.name: Can Safari Profiles use different default search engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

mainEntity.name: Will a school or work device let me change the Safari search engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix search suggestions still showing my old engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

title.rendered: How to check if your iPhone is original, refurbished, or fake in 2026

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways

  • Don’t rely on the serial number alone. A counterfeit device can potentially display identifiers copied from a real iPhone.
  • Check Settings → General → About for the model name, model/part number, serial number, IMEI, carrier information, and iOS version.
  • On supported iPhones, check Parts & Service History for Genuine, Used, Unknown, Unverified, or other repair-related messages.
  • For a second-hand iPhone, make sure Activation Lock is disabled and that the phone can be erased and set up with your own Apple Account.
  • You can also try the *#07# dialer shortcut to reach the Legal & Regulatory information about licensing, warranty information, etc.

Buying an iPhone in 2026 is a little different from buying one a few years ago. Counterfeit phones can copy Apple’s exterior design surprisingly well, while used iPhones can contain replaced displays, batteries, cameras, or other components.

I would no longer depend on the serial number alone for verification purposes. When verifying an iPhone, I look at several things at once, such as device identifiers, Activation Lock status, Parts & Service History, Apple services, and more. This gives a much clearer picture of whether the iPhone is genuine and Apple-certified or has been repaired or modified.

In this article, I will show you under what conditions you should verify your iPhone’s authenticity, and how to check whether your iPhone is original or counterfeit so you can purchase with confidence.

When should you check if an iPhone is original?

I recommend verifying your iPhone’s authenticity before or immediately after buying it, especially in the following situations: 

1. When buying a used or refurbished iPhone

This is probably the most important situation. A used or refurbished iPhone can be completely genuine while still having replacement components. Also, the second-hand market is where most counterfeits appear.

That’s why I don’t stop after checking the serial number. Always verify the device’s Parts & Service History before completing the purchase, even if it looks brand-new. 

2. When the price looks suspiciously low

A very low price doesn’t automatically mean the phone is fake, but it is a reason to investigate further.

If someone offers a brand-new iPhone for half the retail price, it’s likely refurbished, stolen, or fake. So, double-check the model number, serial number, and IMEI before paying.

3. When buying from a marketplace

If you have bought your iPhone on online platforms such as OLX, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, eBay, or from any individual, do not just rely on the Apple-looking box. Verify it the moment you receive it. Many fake or stolen iPhones are sold online disguised as legitimate. 

4. After a repair or replacement

A genuine iPhone can contain non-genuine or previously used replacement components.

If your iPhone has been repaired, especially outside of an Apple Authorized Service Provider (AASP), check that no counterfeit parts were installed. Apple’s “Parts & Service History” feature now lets you confirm this. 

5. If you received the iPhone as a gift or promotion

Even if you didn’t purchase the device yourself, I’d still check it before moving personal data onto it.

Fake iPhones can expose you to security risks, poor performance, and no warranty protection.

Why checking iPhone authenticity matters

A genuine iPhone isn’t just about the Apple logo on the back. 

I want to know that the device:

  • Can receive Apple’s software updates
  • Supports Apple’s security and privacy protections
  • Can use Apple’s official apps and services
  • Doesn’t have an Activation Lock tied to someone else
  • Doesn’t contain unexpected replacement components
  • Has the hardware it claims to have
  • Can be serviced properly through Apple Warranty
  • Isn’t being sold with misleading information

Buying a counterfeit iPhone, which may look real but often fails within months, means wasting your hard-earned money. Moreover, it can expo

10 Ways to check if an iPhone is original or fake in 2026

Here’s a step-by-step guide I use to verify an iPhone’s authenticity. 

1. Check the Serial Number and IMEI

Your iPhone’s IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) and Serial Number are unique identifiers so it’s the easiest way to verify if the iPhone is original. 

To verify your device’s Serial Number: 

  1. Go to Settings → General → About.
  2. Copy the Serial Number. 
  3. Visit Apple’s official warranty checker: checkcoverage.apple.com. 
  4. Enter the serial number and confirm the CAPTCHA.

If Apple recognizes your device as a Valid Purchase and shows warranty details, it’s genuine. Otherwise, if it says “invalid serial number,” the phone is fake or unregistered. 

From the About screen, you can also check the device’s IMEI, Model name, and EID, and compare these details with the original packaging or purchase documentation where applicable. You may also dial *#06# to see the IMEI number.

Important: Don’t treat a recognized serial number as proof. A valid serial number only tells you that the identifier is recognized. However, it does not mean that the device you have physically is the original device associated with that identifier. That’s why I always combine this check with the other methods below.

2. Check the Model and Part Number

Each iPhone model number reveals whether it’s new, refurbished, replaced, or personalized. Find it under Settings → General → About → Model Number. 

  • M – Brand new, purchased retail 
  • F – Refurbished by Apple 
  • N – Replacement for a service request 
  • P – Personalized/engraved by Apple 

Note: These letters appear only in the first character of the part number and may vary slightly by region. 

Now, you may find out if someone is trying to sell you a refurbished phone in the name of a new one. Also, tapping that field reveals the actual model number, which you can compare against the number shown on the box.

3. Check Activation Lock before buying a used iPhone

This is one of the checks I would never skip when buying a second-hand iPhone. A phone can be 100% genuine and still be unusable to you because of Activation Lock.

To check the Activation Lock status, you need to have the device in hand since there’s no way to verify it remotely.

  1. Turn on the iPhone and start the basic setup.
  2. If you see the “iPhone Locked to Owner” screen or the device asks for the previous owner’s Apple Account password, Activation Lock is still enabled.

Apple specifically advises returning an online-purchased iPhone if you see that message. Unless the previous owner properly erases the device and removes it from their account.

4. Check Parts & Service History

Some customers report scams with serviced iPhones. The device is original, but it may have been repaired with non-Apple parts due to malfunctions. So, the iPhone can not provide the same user experience with those parts installed.

Go to Settings → General → About. If the iPhone has repair information available, you’ll see Parts & Service History.

Depending on the iPhone model and component, Apple can show information for parts such as battery, display, logic board, front camera, and rear cameras.

You may see labels such as:

  • Genuine: It means that the repair used genuine Apple parts and processes.
  • Used: The part is a genuine Apple component that was previously used in another iPhone.
  • Unknown: It can indicate a non-genuine component, an installation or verification issue, a malfunctioning component, or a component that has been modified.
  • Unverified: Apple says this can appear when the logic board was previously used in another iPhone. It can affect certain features, including Apple Pay.

So if someone advertises an iPhone as “completely original, never repaired” but Parts & Service History tells a different story, I’d ask questions before buying.

5. Check the iPhone’s physical design

I would recommend checking the device physically because counterfeit manufacturers can imitate software screens, but physical inconsistencies can reveal a lot.

Check:

  • Apple logo placement and polish quality (not printed or glued) 
  • Frame material and finish
  • Button placement
  • Camera arrangement
  • Display bezels and notch
  • Charging port and pentalobe screws near it 
  • Speaker and microphone openings
  • SIM tray, where applicable
  • Overall weight and build quality

Don’t use a generic checklist for every iPhone, though.

For example, newer iPhones have USB-C, while older models use Lightning. Some models have an Action button, while others have a Camera Control button configuration. Camera layouts also vary by generation.

Compare the phone with the specifications and images for the exact iPhone model you’re buying.

6. Use the Legal & Regulatory shortcut

Open the Phone app and enter *#07#, then press the call button.

On supported iPhones, this can take you to the device’s Legal & Regulatory information. You can also open it from Settings → General → Legal & Regulatory.

The screen can contain sections such as:

  • Legal Notices
  • Licence
  • Warranty
  • RF Exposure
  • Safety & Handling
  • Regulatory Certification

It gives you another way to inspect the licence and warranty information associated with the device.

7. Check the iOS Version

A sophisticated counterfeit can imitate the appearance of iOS.

Go to Settings → General → Software Update. The phone should behave like a normal iPhone and provide you with Apple’s software update screen. Here, note the iOS version and build number, and check it against Apple’s official support page.

Also, when you set up your new iPhone, it asks you to create an Apple ID. If it prompts you to enter your Google account or anything else, the iPhone is not original.

However, I wouldn’t use the presence of an iOS-like interface as my only authenticity test. Instead, check whether the device can actually use Apple’s ecosystem and services.

8. Check Apple’s built-in settings and services

A genuine iPhone should provide Apple’s normal system environment, including pre-installed apps and features such as:

  • Settings
  • App Store
  • Safari
  • Messages
  • Photos
  • Phone
  • FaceTime, where available
  • Apple Account services
  • Find My
  • iCloud services

Don’t just look at the icons. Open the apps and settings and make sure the device behaves like an actual iPhone.

If you see an Android-style interface underneath an iOS-like skin, a Google Play Store, or Android system settings, that’s an obvious red flag.

9. Test Face ID, cameras, and connectivity

Before buying a used iPhone, I would spend a few minutes actually testing it.

  • Set up Face ID if the seller allows you to reset the device. If Face ID isn’t working, don’t automatically assume the phone is fake. It could simply have a hardware problem or previous repair.
  • Next, open Camera and test the front camera, rear cameras, zoom levels, video recording, flash, and portrait features.
  • Finally, test Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular network, AirDrop, and NFC-related functions, such as Apple Pay, where available.

A failure here doesn’t prove the phone is counterfeit, but it can reveal hardware or software problems that matter when you’re buying used.

Also, check the battery health of the iPhone. Don’t pay “like-new” money for a phone with a heavily degraded battery.

10. Get it verified by Apple 

In case you still have some doubts about the authenticity of your device, it is advised to get it checked at the nearest Apple Store or Apple Certified Service provider. They can run diagnostics to confirm if your iPhone (and its parts) are authentic Apple components. 

This is particularly useful when you’re dealing with:

  • A suspicious second-hand phone
  • A repaired iPhone
  • A device with Unknown parts
  • Face ID problems
  • A phone with inconsistent identifiers
  • An unusually cheap iPhone
  • A device whose regulatory or model information doesn’t match the seller’s claims

Don’t make these common mistakes

There are several older authenticity tricks I’d no longer treat as definitive.

  • A valid serial number doesn’t prove that the physical hardware is the original device associated with it. Use it together with other checks.
  • Missing Apple Pay or other Apple Intelligence features doesn’t automatically mean the phone is fake. Apple services vary by country, region, device and configuration.
  • Quick Start failure doesn’t prove a counterfeit. It can fail due to normal setup issues or connectivity problems.
  • An “Unknown” part does not necessarily indicate that the whole iPhone is counterfeit. The device itself could be an authentic product from Apple with just one relaced component.

To stay safe, always buy from official Apple Stores or authorized resellers. Avoid deals that seem “too good to be true,” and verify the IMEI and serial number before paying. 

Final thoughts

Checking whether an iPhone is original doesn’t take much time, but it can save you from buying a fake, repaired, or locked device. I recommend checking the serial number, IMEI, Activation Lock, Parts & Service History, software, hardware, and Legal & Regulatory information before making your purchase.

A few minutes of checking can save you from a very expensive mistake. So, is your iPhone really original, or is there something hiding beneath the surface?

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

mainEntity.name: Can Safari Profiles use different default search engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

mainEntity.name: Will a school or work device let me change the Safari search engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix search suggestions still showing my old engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It prevents your number from being displayed through normal Caller ID, but your carrier still knows which number placed the call. Certain emergency or specialized services may also handle caller information differently.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Caller ID hiding only affects voice calls, not SMS or iMessage.

mainEntity.name: Is this supported worldwide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most countries support Caller ID blocking, but availability varies by carrier.

keyPoints.title: When to Verify Your iPhone's Authenticity
keyPoints.explanation: Always check if your iPhone is genuine before or immediately after buying, especially with pre-owned, suspiciously cheap, online, repaired, or gifted devices.

keyPoints.title: Importance of Authenticity Verification
keyPoints.explanation: Verifying your iPhone helps you avoid scams, ensures proper performance and updates, protects your privacy from malware, and guarantees warranty and support eligibility.

keyPoints.title: How to Check IMEI and Serial Number
keyPoints.explanation: Use Settings → General → About to find these numbers, then verify them through Apple’s official website to confirm if the device is recognized as valid and registered.

keyPoints.title: Physical and Internal Checks for Authenticity
keyPoints.explanation: Inspect physical features like build quality, logo placement, and button layout, and verify internal parts and service history through Settings to identify counterfeit or non-genuine components.

keyPoints.title: Additional Verification Methods and Tips
keyPoints.explanation: Test network features, use setup tools like Quick Start and iTunes, confirm iOS and pre-installed apps, activate Siri, and consider getting a professional check at an Apple Store for full verification.

title.rendered: Apple and Qualcomm renew patent license agreement starting in 2027

content.rendered:
Qualcomm has renewed its global patent license agreement with Apple, with the new deal taking effect on April 1, 2027. The announcement does not give the agreement’s duration or financial terms, and it does not announce a new modem-supply deal, according to Qualcomm’s press release.

Patent licensing and buying modem chips are separate arrangements. Qualcomm announced a separate agreement in 2023 to supply Snapdragon 5G Modem-RF Systems for Apple’s smartphone launches in 2024, 2025, and 2026.

Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro introduces its C2 cellular modem system. Our iPhone 18 Pro overview covers the rest of the hardware, while the A20 Pro vs A19 Pro guide explains how a phone’s main processor and cellular modem handle different jobs.

The renewal confirms that Apple’s patent license with Qualcomm continues from April 2027. It does not say which modem chips future iPhones will use. Qualcomm has not shared the length or financial terms of the new license.

excerpt.rendered: Apple and Qualcomm renewed their patent license, effective April 1, 2027. The deal is separate from modem supply; its duration and financial terms remain undisclosed.

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

mainEntity.name: Can Safari Profiles use different default search engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

mainEntity.name: Will a school or work device let me change the Safari search engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix search suggestions still showing my old engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

title.rendered: Apple will fix iPhone 18 Pro Face ID reboot bug with a software update

content.rendered:
Apple told 9to5Mac that a software update will fix a bug that makes some iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max devices freeze and restart after Face ID fails. The update should arrive early next week, according to 9to5Mac’s report.

The issue appears after a failed Face ID attempt when unlocking a protected app, such as Passwords. The phone can stop responding to touch and restart a few seconds later. 9to5Mac reproduced the problem, but it does not affect every iPhone 18 Pro owner.

Apple has not named the update version. 9to5Mac thinks it may be iOS 27.0.1 based on traffic data, but that remains unconfirmed.

The fix is not available yet. When it arrives, iPhone owners can check Settings → General → Software Update or follow our guide to updating an iPhone to iOS 27.

excerpt.rendered: Some iPhone 18 Pro users see their phone freeze and restart after Face ID fails. Apple says a software fix is coming early next week, but has not named the update.

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

title.rendered: Adobe brings creative tools to Gemini and Acrobat editing to Claude

content.rendered:
Adobe is bringing Photoshop, Lightroom, Express, and Firefly tools into Google Gemini, while adding Acrobat tools and hands-on editing to its Claude plugin. The integrations let users work on images, designs, and PDFs inside a chatbot conversation, as Adobe announced on September 24.

Gemini can make and edit creative assets

Adobe in Gemini lets users describe a photo edit, social media asset, or marketing design in chat. Gemini then calls Adobe tools to make the requested changes, such as adjusting product photos, resizing designs for social channels, or personalizing an Express template.

Adobe says the Gemini integration is rolling out globally across Gemini plans. To use it, open Personal Intelligence, choose Adobe under Connected Apps, and sign in to an Adobe account. Adobe’s Gemini connector guide currently lists English as its supported language.

Gemini has been expanding beyond a general-purpose chatbot, with Google’s I/O announcements detailing new AI features across Search, Chrome, and other services. Adobe adds a route from that chat interface to familiar creative tools.

Claude adds PDF and design editing

The Adobe plugin for Claude now includes Acrobat features alongside more than 80 tools from Adobe’s creative apps. Users can combine or split PDFs, delete pages, redact information, and export documents to other formats.

Claude also gets an interactive PDF editor for changing text, reordering pages, and adding comments or highlights. For Adobe Express designs, a layer-based editor lets users adjust individual images, copy, colors, and fonts instead of regenerating the full design.

Adobe says the Claude integration is rolling out globally on Claude and Claude Code for desktop, mobile, and web. People can try it as guests; signing in to Adobe unlocks more tools, higher usage limits, and continuity across sessions.

The new chat integrations add a conversational option to Adobe’s existing apps. People who want to edit directly on their phone can also use the Adobe Photoshop app for iPhone.

excerpt.rendered: Adobe’s Gemini integration brings tools into chat, while its Claude plugin adds Acrobat PDF features and editing controls for documents and Express designs.

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

mainEntity.name: Can Safari Profiles use different default search engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

mainEntity.name: Will a school or work device let me change the Safari search engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix search suggestions still showing my old engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

title.rendered: Collect the Alphabet codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Collect the Alphabet Codes on October 01, 2026

If you’re looking for a Roblox game that’s easy to pick up and play, Collect the Alphabet is worth checking out. The premise is simple: collect all 26 letters, build your own display case, and show off your collection while earning money. However, collecting every letter isn’t as easy as it sounds, as you’ll need to open card packs and gather other resources.

To help players, the developers have released several codes that provide free rewards. So, let’s look at all the Collect the Alphabet codes and how to redeem them.

All working Collect the Alphabet codes

  • GREEK24: 4x Mythic Packs (NEW)
  • UPDATE3: 3x Mythic Packs
  • TIME: 1 2x Mutation Luck Potion
  • VOLCANO: 3x Mythic Packs
  • OPCODE: 3x Double Mutation Luck Potions
  • 1MMEMBERS: 1x Mythic Pack
  • ALPHABET2: 4x Mythic Packs
  • RANDOM: 2x Luck Potion
  • MASTER: 3x Mythic Packs
  • 100KMEMBERS: Redeem this code for 3 Mythic Packs

At the moment, these are the only active Collect the Alphabet codes available to redeem. We’ll keep this list updated and add new codes as soon as the developers release them.

Expired Collect the Alphabet codes

5MVISITS, AURA, NUMBERS, SEPTEMBER, SORRY

  • AURA
  • NUMBERS
  • SEPTEMBER
  • 5MVISITS
  • SORRY

How to redeem Collect the Alphabet codes in Roblox

You might now be wondering how to redeem Collect the Alphabet codes. Thankfully, the process is simple. Follow the steps below to claim your rewards:

  1. Open Collect the Alphabet on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Look at the right side of the screen and click the Settings button.
  4. Scroll down to the Codes box, paste a working code, and click Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed a code, the corresponding rewards should be added to your inventory automatically.

Where to find more Collect the Alphabet codes

The development team behind Collect the Alphabet doesn’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new codes. However, be sure to join the official Collect the Alphabet Discord server, as new codes are often announced there first.

Codes are usually released to celebrate major milestones, updates, or events, so keep an eye on the game’s official Roblox page for the latest announcements.

Be sure to bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated with the latest codes as they’re released. If you enjoy shooting games and want more free rewards, check out the latest The Veil codes, Mog or Die codes, and our complete list of Roblox game codes.

FAQs

How do you get more letters in Collect the alphabet?

You can obtain letters by opening different card packs and spending in-game resources. Keep in mind that some letters are rarer than others, so you may need to keep grinding to find them.

How do you earn money in Collect the Alphabet?

You can earn money by collecting and displaying different letters. Obtaining rarer cards will help increase your earnings.

Why can’t I redeem Collect the Alphabet codes?

If a code isn’t working, make sure you’ve entered it correctly and check whether it has expired. There’s also a chance that you’ve already redeemed it.

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

mainEntity.name: Can Safari Profiles use different default search engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

mainEntity.name: Will a school or work device let me change the Safari search engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix search suggestions still showing my old engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

title.rendered: Birthday Cake in Fortnite: All locations in Battle Royale and OG modes

content.rendered:
The event commemorating Fortnite’s ninth birthday has taken over the game this week, bringing several themed items and quests with it. Among the most prominent of these items are Birthday Cake slices, which you can find across the Fortnite Override map in both Battle Royale and OG modes.

Birthday Cake slices restore health and shields, making them handy consumables during intense matches. At the time of writing, there is also a Fortnite quest that requires you to find and eat a certain number of cake slices, giving you another reason to scour the map for them.

In this article, we cover all the named locations in both Fortnite modes where you can find Birthday Cake slices during the birthday event.

Where to find birthday cake slices in Fortnite Battle Royale

Battle Royale originally had a bug that prevented Birthday Cake slices from spawning on the map, but it has since been fixed. You can now find Birthday Cakes at the seven named locations listed below. There are eight cakes in total, as two can be found in and around Stone Sanctum.

Interestingly, the cakes appear to be spread fairly evenly across the map.

  • Cluster Coast
  • Green Hill Zone
  • Heatwave Harbor
  • Latte Landing
  • Lifty Lodge
  • Stone Sanctum
  • Wonkeeland

Where to find birthday cake slices in Fortnite OG

Compared with Battle Royale, Fortnite OG has a few more locations where you can find Birthday Cake slices. However, the cakes are concentrated in the western, central, and southern parts of the map rather than being evenly distributed.

The following nine points of interest contain Birthday Cakes in OG mode:

  • Fatal Fields
  • Junk Junction
  • Lonely Lodge
  • Loot Lake
  • Paradise Palms
  • Pleasant Park
  • Salty Springs
  • Shifty Shafts
  • Snobby Shores

Keep in mind that Birthday Cakes are limited-time items and will remain available in Fortnite only until October 1. As a result, the locations containing these cakes are likely to be highly contested. Be sure to scan the area for opponents before approaching a cake, and watch your surroundings while your character eats it.

Rounding up

Fortnite’s birthday theme has taken over the game since the beginning of the week, with items such as Balloons, Birthday Presents, and Birthday Cakes becoming part of the gameplay. This refreshing change has influenced how players approach each match and provided more strategic options.

Next Thursday, Epic Games’ multiplayer title will undergo a significant transformation, shifting from a festive atmosphere to a darker setting as Fortnitemares begins. The Halloween-themed event is expected to feature major Fortnite collaborations with horror properties such as Obsession, Child’s Play, It, and Five Nights at Freddy’s, among others.

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

mainEntity.name: Can Safari Profiles use different default search engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

mainEntity.name: Will a school or work device let me change the Safari search engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix search suggestions still showing my old engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

title.rendered: Fortnite 9th Anniversary: All Birthday 2026 quests and rewards

content.rendered:
Fortnite turned 9 in 2026, and the ongoing birthday-themed event, titled “Fortnite Celebration,” kicked off on Monday, September 21, to mark the occasion. As part of the event, several new quests and intriguing birthday party-inspired consumables have arrived in the game, while the Birthday Sprite is also set to arrive soon.

More importantly, there is a range of new anniversary cosmetics that you can obtain by completing certain tasks in Fortnite matches. Thankfully, none of the tasks are too challenging, so most players should be able to complete them with ease.

Below, we list all the birthday celebration-related quest objectives and their corresponding rewards that are available in the game at the time of writing.

Fortnite Celebration quests and rewards list

The following table lists all the available rewards. Some can be obtained by completing individual tasks during gameplay, while others can be unlocked by reaching quest milestones, such as completing a specific number of tasks.

Fortnite Celebration event duration

As with every event, Fortnite Celebration is available for only a limited time and is scheduled to end on October 1. With around a week remaining, the aforementioned quests should be fairly easy to complete before the event ends.

Once Fortnite Celebration concludes, it will be replaced by Fortnitemares, a Halloween-inspired event. Naturally, the upcoming event will have a horror theme, and Fortnite’s official social media channels have already teased its arrival.

Wrapping up

It wouldn’t be wrong to say that Fortnite’s ninth-anniversary celebrations have taken over multiple aspects of the game. From a dedicated sprite to themed quest rewards, the game currently has “birthday mode” written all over it.

Once the ongoing event wraps up, Fortnitemares could take its place as another all-encompassing Fortnite event. In fact, it is already generating considerable anticipation within the community, with players speculating about which major franchises might appear.

Among the IPs rumored to be involved or previously teased and seemingly well suited to the Halloween-themed season are Obsession, Five Nights at Freddy’s, and It.

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

mainEntity.name: Can Safari Profiles use different default search engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

mainEntity.name: Will a school or work device let me change the Safari search engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix search suggestions still showing my old engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

title.rendered: Roblox Slayers 2 codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Slayers 2 Codes on October 12, 2026

For all the Demon Slayer fans out there, there’s a Roblox game you definitely want to check out: Slayers 2. The game lets you choose your path as either a Slayer or a Demon before sending you into an open world filled with quests, weapons, enemies, and plenty of exploration.

Of course, as you progress, you’ll need plenty of resources to level up and skill up your character. Luckily, there are tons of codes that can give you a head start with free rewards. So, let’s take a look at all the working Slayer 2 codes that can give you cash, ores, free spins, and more.

All the working Slayers 2 codes

  • Roguelike: 35 Spins (NEW)
  • ROGUELIKERACERESET: Resets your race (NEW)
  • M1LL1ON: 50 Spins, 10,000 Wen, and 2x Luck
  • Anime Overload
  • Reminiscence Zombies
  • Hot’s RNG

As of now, these are the only active Slayers 2 codes available to redeem. We’ll make sure to keep this list updated and add any new codes as soon as the developers release them.

Expired Slayers 2 codes

ANIM4L, ARTRESET, BREATHRESET, EVILARTSPINS, POINTSRESET, RELEASE26, SKILLTREERESET, SORRYFORSHUTDOWN, SPINS50

  • EVILARTSPINS
  • SORRYFORSHUTDOWN
  • SORRYFORSHUTDOWN

How to redeem Slayers 2 codes in Roblox

The next big question you might be wondering is: how do you redeem Slayers 2 codes? Well, it’s quite a simple process, and we’ve outlined each step below to help you claim your rewards.

  1. Fire up Slayers 2 on Roblox.
  2. Once you’re on the landing page, look for the code redemption box
  3. Paste a working code, and click Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Where to find more Slayers 2 codes

The development team behind Slayers 2 doesn’t have a fixed schedule for dropping codes for the game. However, make sure to join the official Slayers 2 server, as this is the place where new codes are often announced first.

Codes are usually dropped to celebrate major milestones, updates, or events, so keep an eye out on the game’s official page on Roblox for the latest announcements.

Make sure to bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated with the latest codes as they’re released. If you’re into shooting games and want more free rewards, check out the latest The Veil codes, Mog or Die codes, Collect the Alphabet codes and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

FAQs

Why can’t I redeem Slayers 2 codes?

If a Slayers 2 code isn’t working, check if you’ve entered it correctly and that it hasn’t expired. There’s also a chance that you’ve already redeemed the code.

What are Spins used for in Slayers 2?

Spins in Slayers 2 can be used to obtain different rewards and help your character progress.

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

title.rendered: 30+ iPhone settings you should change after updating to iOS 27

content.rendered:
I’ve been using iOS 27 since it launched, and there are quite a few settings I think you should check after updating your iPhone. Some are completely new, while others have been improved with Apple’s latest software.

From Siri AI and Live Translation to smarter Safari tools, expanded parental controls, and new camera options, these settings can help you get more out of your iPhone. If you’re setting up an iPhone 18 Pro, or planning to get the new iPhone Duo, here are the settings I recommend checking first after updating to iOS 27.

1. Turn on Siri AI

Apple has introduced a new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence. Siri AI can understand more natural requests, use personal context, understand what’s on your screen, and perform actions across apps.

For example, instead of giving Siri a simple command, you can ask it to find information buried in your apps, draft an email, or help you work with content on your iPhone.

Siri AI is available in beta on supported Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhones and is currently rolling out in English. Availability varies by language and region.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Siri.
  3. Select Try Siri AI (Beta).
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Apple says Siri AI is available on iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16 models and later, including iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo.

2. Customize Siri’s new voice

iOS 27 also gives Siri AI a more expressive voice experience on supported models.

If you’re using an iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Air, or supported iPhone 17 Pro models, you can adjust Siri’s voice, pace, and expressivity.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Siri.
  3. Tap Voice.
  4. Choose a voice.
  5. Adjust the Pace and Expressivity slider.

If Siri sounds too robotic or too slow for you, this is worth checking.

3. Enable Live Translation in Messages

Live Translation is one of the most useful iOS 27 features if you regularly communicate with people who speak another language. It works in Messages, Phone, and FaceTime, translating conversations in real time. Apple says the feature runs entirely on-device, although availability varies by language and region.

Use Live Translation in Messages

  1. Open the Messages app and tap the conversation you want to translate.
  2. Tap the person’s name at the top of the screen.
  3. Turn on Automatically Translate.
  4. If iPhone doesn’t automatically detect the language, tap Choose Language.
  5. Select the language you want to translate.
  6. Return to the conversation and start typing. Your message will be translated as you type.

When you send it, the recipient receives both the translated message and your original message. Messages you receive are also translated into your preferred language.

Live Translation in Phone calls

You can also use Live Translation during a phone call.

  1. Start a call in the Phone app.
  2. During the call, tap More.
  3. Tap Live Translation.
  4. Choose the language if it isn’t already selected.
  5. Tap Start Translation.
  6. Both people will hear spoken translations, and you can also read an on-screen transcription.

4. Turn on Call Screening

If unknown callers constantly interrupt me, Call Screening is one of the first Phone settings I’d enable.

With Call Screening, iPhone can ask an unknown caller for their name and reason for calling before I decide whether to answer.

How to set it up

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Apps and select Phone.
  3. Scroll to the Screen Unknown Callers section, then choose your preferred option. I have selected Ask Reason for Calling.
  4. You can also toggle on Unknown Callers.

This is particularly useful if you receive lots of calls from numbers you don’t recognize.

5. Turn on Adaptive Power

Adaptive Power is designed to extend battery life by learning how I use my iPhone and automatically adjusting on days when my usage is higher.

Apple introduced Adaptive Power with iOS 26, and it remains relevant for compatible devices in the current iOS generation. Apple says it learns typical battery usage and adjusts the system to help extend battery life.

To enable it, go to Settings → Battery → Power Mode, then toggle on Adaptive Power.

If battery life matters more to you than squeezing out every bit of performance, I’d leave this enabled.

6. Tweak the Liquid Glass effect

If you don’t like the transparency of Apple’s Liquid Glass interface, you don’t have to live with the default appearance.

To reduce transparency:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Appearance.
  3. Select Liquid Glass.
  4. Adjust the slider to make the interface more or less opaque.

I particularly recommend this if transparent menus or backgrounds make text harder to read.

7. Turn off full-screen screenshot previews

iOS continues to display screenshots as full-screen previews by default.

Personally, I prefer the old temporary thumbnail because I often take several screenshots in quick succession.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Tap Screen Capture.
  4. Toggle off Full-Screen Previews.

Apple confirms this setting remains available in iOS 27.

8. Set up automatic Tab organization in Safari

If you usually have dozens of Safari tabs open, iOS 27 can now organize them automatically. Safari’s Topics feature groups your open tabs based on their content, such as Technology, News, or Travel, making them easier to find.

  1. Open Safari and go to the Tab Switcher.
  2. Tap the Filter button at the top.
  3. Tap Organize Tabs.
  4. Select Automatically Create Topics.

Safari will then group your tabs into relevant topics. Tabs that don’t fit a topic will remain separate.

You can also try the Notify Me feature in Safari to get alerts when something changes on a webpage, such as a product becoming available or a price changing.

9. Customize the Action Button

The Action Button remains one of my favorite shortcuts on recent iPhones.

On supported models, it can launch features such as Silent Mode, Camera, Visual Intelligence, Flashlight, Voice Memo, Translate, Magnifier, Shortcuts, and Accessibility.

To customize Action Button:

  1. Open Settings and go to Action Button.
  2. Swipe through the available options and choose the one you use most.

If I were setting up a new iPhone 18 Pro today, I’d definitely revisit this setting rather than leaving it at the default.

10. Customize Camera Control

The iPhone 18 Pro continues to include Camera Control, and iOS 27 gives me more control over how it behaves.

You can access settings such as:

  • Exposure
  • Depth
  • Zoom
  • Cameras
  • Photographic Styles
  • Tone

You can also customize which controls appear and change their order.

  1. Go to Settings → Camera → Camera Control.
  2. Toggle on Camera Adjustments and tap Customize.
  3. Now choose your preferred settings.
  4. Get back and ensure Lock Focus and Exposure is enabled.

Camera Control also provides options to open the native Camera or Instagram Camera with a single click or double-click.

11. Explore the iPhone 18 Pro Camera Controls

If you’ve upgraded to an iPhone 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max, there are several camera settings worth exploring.

The new 48MP Fusion Main camera has a variable aperture with ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, and ƒ/4.0 options. The Pro models also have 48MP Ultra Wide and Telephoto cameras, with up to 8x optical-quality zoom.

Apple also adds Pro controls for:

  • Aperture
  • Shutter speed
  • White balance
  • Histogram
  • Photographic Styles
  • Customizable default lens

You can also put your favorite camera controls above the viewfinder:

  1. Launch Camera and tap the Camera Controls button.
  2. You will see an Edit option at the top.
  3. Add tools such as Timer, Exposure, Styles, Aspect, or Depth, then drag them into the order you want.

12. Turn on Optimized Battery Charging

Optimized Battery Charging is still worth enabling if you plan to keep your iPhone for several years. It learns your charging routine and reduces the amount of time the battery remains fully charged.

  1. Go to Settings → Battery
  2. Tap Charging and toggle on Optimized Battery Charging.

I have set my Charge Limit at 80% to preserve battery lifespan.

13. Turn off personalized ads

If I want to reduce Apple’s use of my activity for ad personalization, I check this setting.

  1. Go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Apple Advertising.
  2. Then turn off Personalized Ads.

Keep in mind that this doesn’t necessarily reduce the number of advertisements you see. It changes how personalized Apple’s ads are.

14. Disable In-App Ratings & Reviews

Those “Rate this app” pop-ups can get annoying.

To stop them:

  1. Open Settings, scroll down, and tap Apps.
  2. Select App Store and toggle off In-App Ratings & Reviews.

I usually turn this off because I prefer leaving reviews when I actually decide to do so.

15. Limit microphone and camera access

I don’t like giving every app unrestricted access to my microphone and camera, so I keep my private moments safe.

  1. Go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone.
  2. Review the apps that have access and disable anything you don’t trust.
  3. Get back and select Camera. Toggle off unnecessary apps.

16. Turn off Lock Screen access to sensitive features

If you’re concerned about someone accessing features while your iPhone is locked, review your Lock Screen access settings.

  1. From Settings, go to Face ID & Passcode.
  2. Enter your passcode to authenticate.
  3. Under Allow Access When Locked, review options such as:
    • Control Center
    • Siri
    • Home Control
    • USB Accessories
    • Reply with Message
    • Wallet

I personally recommend disabling anything you don’t need while the phone is locked.

17. Turn On Find My iPhone

This is one setting I never recommend skipping.

Apple’s Find My app lets you locate your iPhone if it’s misplaced, lost, or stolen. But it only works if Find My iPhone is enabled beforehand. Otherwise, you won’t be able to track your iPhone using Apple’s Find My network.

  1. Go to Settings and tap on your name to access your Apple Account.
  2. Select Find My and tap Find My iPhone.
  3. Turn on:
    • Find My iPhone
    • Find My Network
    • Send Last Location

18. Optimize Storage with High-Efficiency Format

High-quality photos take up a lot of space, and a large collection can quickly strain your iPhone’s storage. Switching to the High-Efficiency format (HEIF/HEVC) reduces file size while maintaining image quality.

  1. Go to Settings → Camera → Formats.
  2. Select High Efficiency.

This is especially useful if you’re taking lots of high-resolution photos and 4K video.

19. Turn off auto-correction

Auto-Correction can be helpful, but I know I’m not the only person who has had an iPhone “correct” a perfectly intentional word.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Keyboard.
  2. Toggle off Auto-Correction if you prefer to control your own typing.

20. Customize dark app icons

If you’re using Dark Mode, I recommend checking your Home Screen customization too.

  1. Touch and hold an empty area on the Home Screen.
  2. Tap the Edit icon at the top.
  3. Tap Customize.
  4. Choose Dark.

You can also explore the other appearance options available in iOS 27.

21. Set up Emergency SOS

I hope you never need this setting, but it’s worth configuring before an emergency happens.

Go to Settings → Emergency SOS, then review options such as:

  • Call with Hold and Release
  • Call with 3 Button Presses
  • Call After Severe Crash

Make sure you have set up emergency contacts.

22. Update parental controls

Apple redesigned Screen Time and added several new controls for parents.

Parents can now use Time Allowances for categories such as Entertainment, Games, and Social Media, while Schedules can control which apps are available at particular times.

To access the new controls, open: Settings→ → Family → [Child’s Name].

From there, you can manage options including:

  • Time Allowances
  • Screen Time Schedules
  • Apps & Websites
  • Communication settings
  • Content restrictions
  • Ask to Browse

Apple says the new Screen Time experience requires the relevant family devices to be updated to iOS 27 or the corresponding new operating systems.

23. Turn on Stolen Device Protection

I strongly recommend checking this after setting up a new iPhone.

Stolen Device Protection adds a one-hour delay when you’re away from trusted locations and requires Face ID to change critical details like your Apple ID password. So, no one can change sensitive settings on your iPhone—even if they know your passcode.

  1. Go to Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Stolen Device Protection.
  2. Then turn it on and set a preferred Require Security Delay option.

24. Hide App Store purchases

There’s always one app you once had on your iPhone, but you don’t want your partner to find out you did. In that case, you can replace the Cloud icon next to the App’s name on the App Store with the Download icon.

Once you’re done, no one will ever know that you downloaded the particular app in the past.

  1. Open the App Store.
  2. Tap your profile picture at the top.
  3. Select Apps & Purchase History.
  4. Tap Your Apps and find the app.
  5. Swipe left and tap Hide.

25. Set up Live Voicemail

Live Voicemail lets you see a transcription of what someone is saying while they’re leaving a voicemail. So, you can decide whether to answer immediately.

  1. Go to Settings → Apps → Phone.
  2. Scroll down and toggle on Live Voicemail

This is useful when I don’t recognize the number but still want to know why someone is calling.

26. Lock private apps

If you have sensitive apps on your iPhone, iOS lets you lock them with Face ID to keep them secure from prying eyes.

  1. Touch and hold the app icon on your Home Screen.
  2. Select Require Face ID.

This is particularly useful for banking, messaging, photo, and note-taking apps.

For better security, I choose Hide and Require Face ID. It moves the app to the Hidden folder in the App Library.

27. Turn on Vehicle Motion Cues

If looking at your iPhone in a moving vehicle makes you feel nauseous, try Vehicle Motion Cues.

  1. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Motion → Vehicle Motion Cues.
  2. Select Automatically in Vehicle.
  3. You can also customize their appearance.

The feature displays animated dots along the edges of the screen that correspond with vehicle movement.

28. Set up a Legacy Contact

With Legacy Contact, you can designate a trusted friend or family member to access your data—like photos, videos, notes, and other important information—after you pass away. This ensures your loved ones can preserve cherished memories.

How to set it up:

  1. Open Settings and go to Apple Account → Sign-In & Security → Legacy Contact.
  2. Tap Add Legacy Contact and choose someone you trust.
  3. Follow the setup process.

29. Turn off App Tracking

I recommend reviewing app tracking permissions after every major iOS update.

Many apps track your activity across websites and other apps to build profiles and serve targeted ads. Disabling tracking stops this data collection, protecting your privacy.

  1. Go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking and toggle off unnecessary apps.
  2. You can disable Allow Apps to Request to Track completely or review individual apps.

30. Review Background App Refresh

Background App Refresh can be useful, but I don’t necessarily need every app updating in the background.

Disabling Background App Refresh saves battery, reduces data usage, and boosts performance by stopping apps from updating when not in use.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Background App Refresh.
  2. Select Background App Refresh.
  3. You can turn it off completely or enable it only for Wi-Fi.

I prefer reviewing the app list and disabling unnecessary ones rather than automatically turning the feature off for everything.

31. Customize Lock Screen controls

iOS lets you replace the default Lock Screen controls with other options.

  1. Touch and hold the Lock Screen.
  2. Tap Customize.
  3. Tap the minus (-) button to remove a control.
  4. Tap + to choose another control.

This can be a convenient place to put shortcuts to the features you use regularly.

32. Enable Screen Distance

Screen Distance can warn you when you hold your iPhone too close to your face for an extended period. It helps reduce eye strain and the risk of myopia.

  1. Go to Settings → Screen Time.
  2. Select Content & Privacy Restrictions.
  3. Tap Screen Distance and toggle it off.

If you’re comfortable with the feature, I’d leave it enabled. If you find the warnings disruptive, you can turn it off here.

33. Enable Reduce Loud Audio

Finally, if you frequently use AirPods or headphones, check your headphone safety settings.

  1. Go to Settings → Sounds & Haptics → Headphone Safety → Reduce Loud Audio.
  2. Then choose a decibel limit.

This can help prevent headphone audio from exceeding the level you’ve selected.

iPhone experience enhanced!

iOS 27 is much more than another visual update. Apple has pushed Siri much further, expanded Apple Intelligence into everyday apps, added useful Safari automation, introduced new parental controls, and made the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera hardware more configurable.

The biggest change for me is that the iPhone is becoming more context-aware. Siri can work with what I’m typing, what’s on my screen, what’s in my camera view, and information inside my apps.

And with iPhone Duo arriving October 23, Apple’s iOS experience is about to extend to a completely new form factor.

If you’ve just installed iOS 27, I wouldn’t change every setting on this list blindly. Instead, go through it once and enable the features that actually fit the way you use your iPhone.

Which iOS 27 feature did you like the most?

mainEntity.name: How can I set a different search engine for Private Browsing in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a Mac, open Safari, select Settings, then choose Search, and use the "Private Browsing search engine" dropdown. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Safari > Private Search Engine, located just below the primary Search Engine setting, and select your preferred option.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Safari search engine option greyed out on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means Screen Time restrictions are active. Go to Settings, Screen Time, Content & Privacy Restrictions, adjust Web Content or turn the switch off.

mainEntity.name: Which search engines are available in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari typically offers Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, and Yahoo, although availability varies by region.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the Safari engine affect Spotlight or Siri search results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This only changes Safari's address bar, while Spotlight and Siri continue to use their own systems.

mainEntity.name: Can Safari Profiles use different default search engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The search engine setting applies across all profiles, although you can still visit a different engine's homepage or use a bookmark within each profile when needed.

mainEntity.name: Will a school or work device let me change the Safari search engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your organization's device management policies. Managed devices may block this setting.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix search suggestions still showing my old engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear Safari history and website data in Settings, Safari, Clear History and Website Data, then force quit and relaunch Safari. On Mac, Safari's Clear History feature also works.

mainEntity.name: Does hiding the Caller ID hide my number from everyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It prevents your number from being displayed through normal Caller ID, but your carrier still knows which number placed the call. Certain emergency or specialized services may also handle caller information differently.

mainEntity.name: Will text messages show my number?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Caller ID hiding only affects voice calls, not SMS or iMessage.

mainEntity.name: Does hiding Caller ID work with FaceTime?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. FaceTime has separate Caller ID controls. You can choose whether your phone number or Apple Account email address is used for FaceTime Caller ID in Settings > Apps > FaceTime.

mainEntity.name: Is this supported worldwide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most countries support Caller ID blocking, but availability varies by carrier.
